name: Deuteronomy
sourceNote: Translated from the Hebrew of the Westminster Leningrad Codex, checked against the Samaritan Pentateuch, the Septuagint, the Dead Sea Scrolls of Deuteronomy, and the Nash Papyrus as reported in general terms. Every Septuagint reading cited in the footnotes was checked against Brenton’s public-domain English translation of the Septuagint. Readings of the Samaritan Pentateuch, the Dead Sea Scrolls, and other ancient versions are stated in general terms until they can be checked against the critical editions. Verse numbers follow the standard English Bible; where the Hebrew numbering differs (12:32, 22:30, and 29:1 in English are 13:1, 23:1, and 28:69 in Hebrew, and the following verses shift accordingly), a footnote says so. Measurements are given in modern US units, and dates use approximate modern months, with the originals in the footnotes.

verses.text: These are the words that Moses addressed to all Israel across the Jordan, in the wilderness, in the Arabah{a} facing Suph,{b} in the region between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Di-zahab.{c}
It is an eleven-day journey from Horeb{d} by the Mount Seir road to Kadesh-barnea.
In the fortieth year, in the eleventh month (in January–February), on the first day of the month,{e} Moses spoke to the Israelites, telling them everything Yahweh{f} had commanded him to tell them.
He spoke after he had struck down Sihon, the Amorite king who ruled from Heshbon, and Og, the king of Bashan who ruled from Ashtaroth and{g} from Edrei.
Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses undertook to explain this instruction.{h} He said:
“At Horeb Yahweh our God said to us: ‘You have lived long enough at this mountain.

Turn and set out. Go to the hill country of the Amorites and to all their neighbors in the Arabah, the hill country, the Shephelah,{i} the Negev,{j} and the seacoast—the land of the Canaanites—and to Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates.
Look, I have laid the land open before you. Go in and take over the land that Yahweh swore{k} he would give to your forefathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and to their offspring after them.’
“At that time I told you, ‘I cannot carry you by myself.
Yahweh your God has increased your numbers, and look, today you are as countless as the stars of heaven.
May Yahweh, the God of your ancestors, make you a thousand times as many as you are now and bless you as he promised you!
How can I alone bear the weight and burden of you and your quarrels?
Pick men from each of your tribes who are wise, discerning, and well known, and I will make them your heads.’
You replied to me, ‘The thing you have spoken of doing is good.’
So I took the heads of your tribes, wise and well-known men, and made them heads over you—commanders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens—and officials for your tribes.
At that time I charged your judges: ‘Hear the cases between your fellow Israelites{l} and decide rightly between a man and his brother, or the foreigner who lives with him.
Show no favoritism in judgment; hear the small and the great alike. Fear no one, for the judgment is God’s. Any case too hard for you, bring to me, and I will hear it.’
I gave you orders at that time about everything you were to do.

“Then we set out from Horeb and went through all that vast and terrible wilderness you saw, on the way to the hill country of the Amorites, as Yahweh our God had commanded us, and we came to Kadesh-barnea.
I said to you, ‘You have come to the hill country of the Amorites, which Yahweh our God is giving us.
Look, Yahweh your God has set the land before you. Go up and take it, as Yahweh, the God of your ancestors, has told you. Do not fear or lose heart.’
“Then you all approached me and said, ‘We should send men on ahead to explore the land for us and to bring back a report on the route we should take up and the cities we will reach.’
The idea pleased me, so I chose twelve men from among you, a man for each tribe.
They turned and went up into the hill country, came to the Valley of Eshcol,{m} and spied it out.
They took some of the land’s fruit in their hands, brought it down to us, and reported, ‘The land Yahweh our God is giving us is good.’
“Yet you would not go up. You rebelled against the command of Yahweh your God.
You complained in your tents and said, ‘Because Yahweh hates us he brought us out of the land of Egypt, to hand us over to the Amorites to wipe us out.

Where are we going up to? Our brothers have made our hearts melt. They say, “The people are greater and taller than we are; the cities are great and walled up to the sky. And we saw the sons of the Anakim{n} there.”’
“I said to you, ‘Do not dread them or fear them.
Yahweh your God, who is going ahead of you, is the one who will fight on your behalf, exactly as he did for you in Egypt, before your very eyes,
and in the wilderness, where you saw how Yahweh your God bore you as a father bears his child, all along the way you walked until you reached this place.’
Yet in this matter you did not trust Yahweh your God,
who went before you on the way to seek out a place for you to camp, in fire by night to show you the road you should take, and in the cloud by day.
“Yahweh heard the sound of your words and was angry, and he swore:
‘Not a single man of this wicked generation shall look on the good land that I swore to give your forefathers,
save Caleb{o} the son of Jephunneh; he shall see it, and I will give him and his sons the land on which he walked, because he wholly followed Yahweh.’
Even with me Yahweh was angry because of you, and he said, ‘You also will not go in there.
Joshua{p} son of Nun, who stands before you, he will go in there. Strengthen him, for he will make Israel inherit it.
Your little ones, about whom you said they would be taken as spoil,{q} and your sons, who as yet have no understanding of good or bad, will enter it; to them I will give it, and they will inherit it.
But you, turn back and set out into the wilderness by way of the Red Sea.’{r}

“Then you answered me, ‘We have sinned against Yahweh. We ourselves will go up and fight, in keeping with all that Yahweh our God commanded us.’ So every man girded on his weapons of war, regarding the ascent into the hill country as a trifle.
But Yahweh told me, ‘Tell them, “Do not go up, and do not fight, because I am not among you; otherwise your enemies will defeat you.”’
I spoke to you, but you would not listen. You rebelled against Yahweh’s command, and in your presumption you went up into the hill country.
Then the Amorites who lived in that hill country came out against you and chased you as bees do, and beat you down from Seir{s} as far as Hormah.
So you returned and wept before Yahweh; but Yahweh would not hear your voice, nor give ear to you.
So you remained at Kadesh many days, as many days as you remained there.

notes.text: The Arabah is the great rift valley running south from the Sea of Galilee, through the Jordan Valley and the Dead Sea, down to the Gulf of Aqaba.
Hebrew Suph, “reeds,” perhaps short for Yam Suph, the Sea of Reeds; the Septuagint has “near the Red Sea.” The locations of the places named in this verse are uncertain.
Di-zahab means “abundance of gold”; the Septuagint translates it “the gold works.” Paran perhaps means “place of caves”; Laban means “white”; Hazeroth means “enclosures” or “villages.”
Horeb (perhaps “dry” or “desolate”) is the name Deuteronomy usually gives to the mountain called Sinai in Exodus. Kadesh-barnea: Kadesh means “holy.”

Hebrew “in the eleventh month,” later called Shevat. This translation counts the months from the spring new year (Nisan, also called Abib, in March–April). The Hebrew calendar is lunar, so modern equivalents are approximate.
Yahweh is the personal name of Israel’s God (Hebrew YHWH), which many English versions replace with “the LORD”; see Exodus 3:14–15. Moses means “drawn out” (Exodus 2:10).

So the Septuagint (compare Joshua 12:4); the Hebrew lacks “and.” Sihon’s name may mean “sweeping away”; Og’s is of uncertain meaning; Heshbon means “reckoning”; Ashtaroth is named for the goddess Astarte; Edrei may mean “strength.”
Or “law.” Hebrew torah means instruction or teaching, and in Deuteronomy it often refers to the body of teaching Moses gives.
The Shephelah (“lowland”) is the band of low hills between the central highlands and the coastal plain.
The Negev (“dry land”) is the arid south of the land.
Hebrew “that Yahweh swore to your fathers.” The Septuagint reads “which I swore,” and other ancient witnesses are reported to agree.
Hebrew “your brothers,” here and often in Deuteronomy for fellow members of the people of Israel.
Eshcol means “cluster” (of grapes); see Numbers 13:23–24. The Septuagint translates the name “the valley of the cluster.”
The Anakim were a people remembered for their great size; Anak may mean “long-necked.” The Septuagint has “the sons of the giants.”
Caleb probably means “dog,” perhaps in the sense of a faithful servant; Jephunneh is of uncertain meaning.
Joshua means “Yahweh saves.” Nun may mean “fish”; the Septuagint spells the name “Naue.”
The Septuagint lacks “who you said would become plunder.”
Hebrew Yam Suph, “Sea of Reeds,” here probably the Gulf of Aqaba.
So the Septuagint and other ancient versions; the Hebrew reads “in Seir.” Hormah means “destruction” or “place devoted to destruction.”

verses.text: “Then we turned and set out into the wilderness by way of the Red Sea, as Yahweh had told me, and for many days we went around Mount Seir.
“Then Yahweh said to me,
‘You have been going around this hill country long enough. Turn north.
Give the people this order: “You are about to pass along the border of your kinsmen, Esau’s descendants,{a} who live in Seir. They will be afraid of you, so be very careful.
Do not start a fight with them, for I will not give you any of their land, not so much as a footprint, because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as his own.
You are to buy the food you eat from them with silver, and you are also to buy the water you drink from them with silver.

For Yahweh your God has blessed you in all that your hands have done. He has known your going through this great wilderness. For these forty years Yahweh your God has been with you; you have lacked nothing.”’
“So we went on past our kinsmen, the sons of Esau, who dwell in Seir, away from the Arabah road, away from Elath and Ezion Geber.{b} And we turned and traveled the way of the wilderness of Moab.
Yahweh told me, ‘Do not treat Moab as an enemy or go to war with them. I will not give you any part of their land to own, because I have assigned Ar{c} to Lot’s descendants{d} as their own.’
(The Emim{e} lived there formerly, a people great and many and tall as the Anakim.
They also were reckoned as Rephaim,{f} like the Anakim, but the Moabites call them Emim.
The Horites{g} also used to live in Seir, but Esau’s descendants dispossessed them, wiped them out, and took over their land, just as Israel was to do in the land Yahweh gave them to own.)
‘Now get up and cross the Wadi Zered.’{h} So we crossed the Wadi Zered.
We spent thirty-eight years getting from Kadesh-barnea to the crossing of the Wadi Zered. By then that whole generation of soldiers had died out of the camp, as Yahweh had sworn to them.
Indeed, the hand of Yahweh was against them, to root them out from the midst of the camp until they had perished.
“When all the men of war had died and were gone from among the people,
Yahweh spoke to me:
‘Today you are crossing the border of Moab at Ar.

And when you approach the border of the Ammonites, do not harass them or provoke them to battle; for I will give you no part of the Ammonites’ land as a possession, since I have given it to the sons of Lot for a possession.’
(That also is reckoned a land of Rephaim. Rephaim lived there formerly, but the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,{i}
a people great and many and tall as the Anakim. But Yahweh destroyed them before the Ammonites, and they drove them out and settled in their place,
just as he had done for Esau’s descendants who live in Seir, when he wiped out the Horites ahead of them; they dispossessed them and occupy their land to this day.
And the Avvim,{j} who lived in villages as far as Gaza, were wiped out by the Caphtorim,{k} who had come from Caphtor and then took over their land.)
‘Get up, set out, and cross the Arnon Valley.{l} See, I have put into your hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin to take possession; fight him in battle.
This day I will begin to put the dread and fear of you on the peoples everywhere under heaven. When they hear the report of you, they will tremble and writhe in anguish because of you.’
“So I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth{m} to Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace:
‘Let me pass through your land. I will go only along the road; I will turn neither to the right nor to the left.
Sell me food for silver so that I may eat, and give me water for silver so that I may drink. Only let me go through on foot,
Esau’s descendants in Seir did this for me, and so did the Moabites in Ar. Let me go on until I have crossed the Jordan into the land Yahweh our God is giving us.’
But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass by him, for Yahweh your God had hardened his spirit and made his heart stubborn, in order to give him into your hand, as he is today.
Then Yahweh said to me, ‘See, I have begun to give Sihon and his land over to you. Begin to take possession, so that you may possess his land.’
Sihon came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Jahaz.
But Yahweh our God gave him up to us, and we defeated him, his sons,{n} and all his people.
We captured all his cities at that time and devoted{o} every city to destruction, men and women and little ones. We left no survivor.
Only the livestock we took as plunder for ourselves, with the spoil of the cities we had captured.
From Aroer on the rim of the Arnon gorge, and from the city in the gorge, as far as Gilead, no town was too lofty for us; Yahweh our God handed over all of them to us.
Only you did not go near the land of the Ammonites, the whole bank of the Jabbok River,{p} or the cities of the hill country, or any place Yahweh our God had forbidden.

notes.text: Esau means “hairy”; see Genesis 25:25. Seir also suggests “hairy,” perhaps of its wooded slopes.
Elath (“terebinth”) and Ezion-geber were at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba.
Ar (“city”) was a city or district of Moab.
Lot may mean “covering.” Moab and Ammon descended from him (Genesis 19:36–38).
Emim means “terrors.”
The Rephaim were an ancient people remembered as giants; the same word elsewhere means the “shades” of the dead.
The Horites may be “cave dwellers,” or the name may refer to the Hurrians.
Hebrew nahal, a valley with a stream that flows mainly in the rainy season. Zered may mean “willow” or “luxuriant growth.”
Zamzummim may mean “murmurers”; the meaning is uncertain.
Avvim may mean “ruins.”
Caphtor is usually identified with Crete; the Philistines came from there (Amos 9:7).
The Arnon is the gorge east of the Dead Sea that formed Moab’s northern border; its name may mean “roaring stream.”
Kedemoth means “eastern places.” Jahaz (verse 32) may mean “trodden place.”
So the Hebrew reading tradition (qere); the written text (ketiv) has “his son.”
Hebrew herem: to give something over completely to God, which in war meant its total destruction.
The Jabbok, perhaps “flowing,” is a tributary that runs west into the Jordan.

verses.text: “Then we turned and went up the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.

But Yahweh told me, ‘Have no fear of him, for into your hand I have given him, his whole people, and his land; deal with him as you dealt with Sihon, king of the Amorites, who made his home in Heshbon.’
So Yahweh our God also delivered into our hands Og the king of Bashan with all his people; we struck them down until not one was left of them.
At that time we took all his cities; not one of the towns was left that we did not seize from them—sixty cities, the entire district of Argob,{a} Og’s kingdom in Bashan.
All these were cities fortified with high walls, gates, and bars, besides a great many open villages.
We devoted them to destruction, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, devoting every city to destruction, men, women, and little ones.
But all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we took as plunder for ourselves.
“So at that time we took the land out of the hand of the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon{b}
(the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir),
all the cities of the plateau, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan, to Salecah and Edrei, the cities of Og’s kingdom in Bashan.

(For only Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. Look, his bed{c} was a bed of iron. Is it not still in Rabbah of the Ammonites? It is about thirteen and a half feet long and six feet wide, measured by a man’s forearm.{d})

“This is the land that we took possession of at that time: from Aroer, on the edge of the Arnon gorge, and half of the hill country of Gilead with its cities, I gave to the Reubenites and the Gadites.
The rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh. (The whole region of Argob, all that Bashan, is called a land of Rephaim.
Jair{e} the Manassite captured all the Argob region up to the Geshurite and Maacathite frontier, and he named Bashan after himself, Havvoth-jair,{f} the name it still has today.)
To Machir{g} I gave Gilead.

To the tribes of Reuben and Gad I assigned the land stretching from Gilead down to the Arnon Valley (the middle of the gorge forming the boundary) and up to the Jabbok River, which is the Ammonite border,
and also the Arabah, with the Jordan as a border, from Chinnereth{h} as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea,{i} under the slopes of Pisgah{j} to the east.
“At that time I commanded you: ‘Yahweh your God has given you this land to possess. All you who are fit for war shall cross over armed before your fellow Israelites.
Only your wives, your little ones, and your livestock (I know that you have much livestock) shall stay in the towns I have given you,

until Yahweh gives your kinsmen rest as he has given you, and they too take over the land Yahweh your God is giving them across the Jordan. After that, every man may go back to the property I have given him.’
“And at that time I charged Joshua: ‘Your own eyes have seen everything Yahweh your God did to these two kings; Yahweh will do the same to all the kingdoms through which you will pass.
Do not fear them, for it is Yahweh your God who fights for you.’
“At that time I begged Yahweh for mercy:

‘Lord Yahweh,{k} you have begun to let your servant see your greatness and your strong hand. Is there a god anywhere in the heavens or on the earth whose works and mighty deeds can compare with yours?
Let me cross over, I pray, and see the good land on the other side of the Jordan—that fine hill country, and the Lebanon.’
But Yahweh was angry with me because of you and would not listen to me. Yahweh said to me, ‘Enough from you! Speak to me no more of this matter.
Climb to the summit of Pisgah and look around, westward, northward, southward, and eastward. Look at it well with your own eyes, because you will not cross this Jordan.
Give Joshua his orders, encourage him, and make him strong, because he is the one who will cross over leading this people, and he is the one who will hand over to them the land you are about to see.’
And so we stayed on in the valley facing Beth-peor.{l}

notes.text: Argob may mean “heap of stones.”
Hermon means “sacred” or “devoted.” Sirion and Senir may both mean “breastplate,” perhaps from the mountain’s shining snow.
Or “his coffin” or “sarcophagus”; the Hebrew word usually means a bed or couch.
Hebrew “nine cubits its length and four cubits its width, by the cubit of a man,” about 4 by 1.8 meters. A cubit was about 18 inches (45 centimeters).
Jair means “he gives light.”
Havvoth-jair means “tent villages of Jair.”
Machir means “sold.” He was Manasseh’s son (Genesis 50:23); Manasseh means “causing to forget” (Genesis 41:51).
Chinnereth (perhaps “harp-shaped”) is the Sea of Galilee.
The Dead Sea.
Pisgah is a ridge of the Abarim mountains northeast of the Dead Sea, near Mount Nebo.
Hebrew Adonai YHWH.
Beth-peor means “house of Peor,” a place linked with the worship of the Baal of Peor (Numbers 25).

verses.text: “And now, Israel, listen to the statutes and the rulings I am teaching you to do, so that you may live, and go in and possess the land that Yahweh, the God of your ancestors, is giving you.
Do not add to the word I command you or take anything from it, so that you may keep the commands of Yahweh your God that I am giving you.
Your own eyes saw what Yahweh did at Baal-peor.{a} Every man who went after the Baal of Peor, Yahweh your God wiped out from among you,
but all of you who clung to Yahweh your God are alive today.
See, I have taught you statutes and rulings, as Yahweh my God commanded me, for you to do in the land you are entering to possess.

Guard them and practice them, because this will show your wisdom and good sense to the nations. Hearing of all these statutes, they will exclaim, ‘What a wise and discerning people this great nation is!’
For what great nation is there that has gods so near to it as Yahweh our God is to us whenever we call to him?
Or what great nation has statutes and ordinances so just as this whole law which I set before you today?

“But be on your guard, and watch yourself carefully, so you will not forget what you have seen with your own eyes, or let it slip from your mind for as long as you live. Teach it to your children and to their children.

Remember the day you stood in the presence of Yahweh your God at Horeb, when Yahweh told me, ‘Call the people together to me, so that I may have them hear my words, that they may learn to revere me for as long as they live on the earth, and may teach their children so.’
You drew near and stood at the base of the mountain, and the mountain was ablaze with fire reaching into the very heart of the sky, wrapped in darkness, cloud, and thick gloom.
Then Yahweh spoke to you out of the fire. You heard words being spoken, but you saw no shape—only a voice.
He declared to you his covenant, which he commanded you to perform, the Ten Words,{b} and he wrote them on two tablets of stone.
And Yahweh commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and rulings, for you to do them in the land you are crossing into to possess.
“Therefore be very careful about yourselves, since you saw no form on the day Yahweh spoke to you at Horeb out of the midst of the fire,
so that you do not act corruptly by making yourselves a carved image, in the form of any figure, the likeness of male or female,
the likeness of any beast that is on the earth, the likeness of any winged bird that flies in the sky,
the likeness of anything that creeps on the ground, the likeness of any fish that is in the water under the earth.

And take heed lest you lift your eyes to heaven and see the sun, the moon, and the stars, the whole host of heaven, and be drawn away to worship and serve them—those Yahweh your God has assigned to all the nations under all of heaven.
But Yahweh has taken you and brought you out from Egypt, the iron smelting furnace, to be his own people, his inheritance, as you are today.
But Yahweh was angry with me on your account and swore that I would not go across the Jordan or come into the good land that Yahweh your God is giving you to inherit.
For I will die in this land, without crossing the Jordan; but you will go over and inherit this good land.
Take care not to forget the covenant of Yahweh your God that he made with you, and do not make yourselves a carved image in the form of anything Yahweh your God has forbidden you.
For Yahweh your God is a fire that consumes, a jealous God.
“After you have had children and grandchildren and have grown old in the land, if you then become corrupt and make an idol in any shape, and do evil in the sight of Yahweh your God and provoke him,

I summon heaven and earth today to testify against you: you will quickly vanish from the land you are about to cross the Jordan to take over. You will not live there long; you will be completely wiped out.
Yahweh will scatter you among the peoples, and you will be left few in number among the nations where Yahweh will drive you.
There you will serve gods that are the work of human hands, wood and stone, which neither see nor hear nor eat nor smell.
But from there you will search for Yahweh your God, and you will find him, provided you seek him with your whole heart and your whole being.
When you are in distress and all these things have found you in the latter days, you will return to Yahweh your God and obey his voice.
For Yahweh your God is a merciful God. He will not fail you or ruin you, and he will not forget the covenant he made with your forefathers and confirmed by oath.

“Go on, ask about the days long past, the ages before you, back to the day God created humankind{c} on the earth. Ask from one horizon of the sky to the other: has any event as great as this ever taken place? Has anyone ever heard of such a thing?
Has any people ever heard the voice of a god{d} speaking from the middle of the fire, as you have heard, and still lived?

Or has any god ever tried to go and take a nation for himself from within another nation, by trials, by signs, by wonders, by war, by a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and by great terrors, according to all that Yahweh your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?
To you it was shown, so that you might know that Yahweh, he is God; there is no other besides him.
From the sky he let you hear his voice so as to instruct you, and on the earth he let you see his great fire, and out of that fire you heard his words.
Because he loved your forefathers, he chose their offspring after them, and he himself, in person{e} and in great strength, brought you out of Egypt,
to drive out ahead of you nations bigger and stronger than you, to bring you in and hand over their land to you as your inheritance, as is now happening.
Know therefore today, and lay it to your heart, that Yahweh, he is God in heaven above and on the earth beneath; there is no other.

Keep his statutes and his commands, which I command you today, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you, and so that you may prolong your days in the land that Yahweh your God is giving you for all time.”
Then Moses set apart three cities beyond the Jordan, toward the sunrise,
so that anyone who killed his neighbor unintentionally, without having hated him in the past, could flee there, and by fleeing to one of these cities he might live:
Bezer, in the desert on the tableland, belonged to the Reubenites; Ramoth in Gilead to the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan to the Manassites.{f}
This is the instruction{g} that Moses set before the Israelites.
These are the testimonies, the statutes, and the rulings that Moses spoke to the Israelites when they came out of Egypt,
across the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth Peor, in the territory of Sihon, the Amorite king who ruled from Heshbon, whom Moses and the Israelites had overcome as they were leaving Egypt.
They took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise,
It stretched from Aroer, at the rim of the Arnon gorge, to Mount Sion{h} (that is, Hermon),
as well as all the Arabah on the east side of the Jordan down to the Sea of the Arabah, beneath the slopes of Pisgah.

notes.text: Baal-peor means “lord of Peor.” See Numbers 25:1–9.
Hebrew “the ten words,” the Ten Commandments (also 10:4). See 5:6–21.
Or “Adam.” Hebrew ʾadam, “humankind,” which is also the name of the first man.
Or “the voice of God.” The Septuagint reads “the voice of the living God.”
Hebrew “with his face.”
Bezer means “fortress”; Ramoth means “heights”; Golan may mean “circle” or “exile.” Gilead may mean “heap of witness” (Genesis 31:47–48).
Or “law.” Hebrew torah.
Hebrew Siʾon, a different name from Zion in Jerusalem. The Syriac reads “Sirion” (compare 3:9).

verses.text: Moses summoned all Israel and said to them: “Listen, Israel, to the statutes and rulings I am announcing in your hearing today. Learn them, and be careful to carry them out.
Yahweh our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
Yahweh did not make this covenant with our ancestors, but with us, we who are all of us here alive this day.
Face to face Yahweh spoke with you on the mountain, out of the fire.
(At that time I was standing between Yahweh and you to relay Yahweh’s word to you, since the fire frightened you and you would not climb the mountain.) He said:
‘I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house where you were slaves.{a}{b}
‘You shall have no other gods before me.{c}
‘Do not make yourself a carved image, the likeness{d} of anything in the sky overhead, on the earth beneath, or in the water below the earth.

Do not bow down to them or worship them, for I, Yahweh your God, am a jealous God, holding children to account for the wrongdoing of their fathers, to the third and the fourth generation of those who hate me,
yet I show steadfast love{e} for a thousand generations{f} to those who love me and keep my commands.
‘You shall not take up the name of Yahweh your God for an empty purpose,{g} for Yahweh will not hold guiltless whoever takes up his name for an empty purpose.
‘Keep the Sabbath day{h} holy by observing it, just as Yahweh your God commanded you.
Six days you are to labor and do all your work,

Yet the seventh day is a Sabbath belonging to Yahweh your God. On it you shall do no work at all: you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, your ox, your donkey, any of your livestock, or the sojourner living inside your gates; that your male servant and female servant may rest as well as you.

Remember that you yourself were a slave in the land of Egypt, and that Yahweh your God brought you out of there by a strong hand and an outstretched arm. That is why Yahweh your God has commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.{i}
‘Honor your father and your mother, as Yahweh your God commanded you, so that your days may be long and that it may go well with you on the soil that Yahweh your God is giving you.{j}
‘You shall not murder.{k}
‘And you shall not commit adultery.
‘And you shall not steal.
‘And you shall not testify against your neighbor as an empty{l} witness.
‘And you shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, and you shall not crave your neighbor’s house or field, his slave, male or female, his ox or donkey, or anything at all that is your neighbor’s.’{m}

“These are the words Yahweh spoke with a mighty voice to your whole assembly on the mountain, out of the fire, the cloud, and the dense darkness, and he said nothing more. He wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
But when you heard the voice out of the darkness, while the mountain was ablaze with fire, you came to me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders,

and you said, ‘See, Yahweh our God has shown us his glory and his greatness, and we heard his voice from the midst of the fire; today we have seen that God may speak with a person, and that person lives on.
But now, why should we die? This great fire will devour us. If we go on hearing the voice of Yahweh our God any longer, we will die.
For what mortal{n} has ever heard the living God’s voice speak from out of the fire, as we did, and still lived?
You go near and hear all that Yahweh our God says. Then you tell us everything that Yahweh our God tells you, and we will hear and do it.’
“Yahweh heard what you said to me, and Yahweh said to me, ‘I have heard the words that this people spoke to you. All that they have spoken is well said.
If only their hearts were always set like this, to fear me and keep all my commands, so that they and their children might prosper forever!
Go and say to them, “Go back to your tents.”
But you, stand here beside me, and I will tell you the whole command, the statutes and the rulings, that you shall teach them, so they will do them in the land I am giving them to possess.’
Take care, then, to act as Yahweh your God has commanded you. Do not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.
Walk in the whole way that Yahweh your God has commanded you, so that you may live and prosper and have long life in the land you are going to possess.

notes.text: Verses 6–21 give the Ten Words (4:13) in a form close to Exodus 20:2–17; the main differences are noted at verses 8, 11, 12, 15, 16, 17, 20, and 21. Jewish and Christian traditions divide the Ten Words in different ways; the paragraphing here follows the commands, not any one numbering.

The Nash Papyrus, a single sheet bought in Egypt and usually dated to the second or first century BC, contains a Hebrew text of the Ten Words followed by the Shema (6:4–5). Before the Dead Sea Scrolls were found, it was the oldest known Hebrew biblical manuscript. Its text of the Ten Words is reported to blend the forms of Exodus 20 and Deuteronomy 5 (for example, it gives the creation reason for the Sabbath found in Exodus 20:11) and to place the command against adultery before the command against murder. These details should be checked against a critical edition.
Or “besides me” or “in addition to me”; Hebrew “before my face.”
Exodus 20:4 reads “or any likeness”; here the Hebrew has no “or,” so the second phrase may explain the first. Some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient versions are reported to read “or” here as well.
Hebrew hesed, loyal and faithful love, especially within a covenant.
Or “to thousands.”
Or “in vain” or “to deceive”; Hebrew “lift up the name … to emptiness.”
Exodus 20:8 reads “Remember the Sabbath day.” Sabbath means “ceasing” or “rest.”

In Exodus 20:11 the reason given for the Sabbath is that Yahweh rested on the seventh day of creation. Here the reason is Israel’s release from slavery, and verse 14 adds the ox, the donkey, and the rest for slaves.
The words “as Yahweh your God commanded you” and “that it may go well with you” are not in Exodus 20:12.
Hebrew ratsah, the unlawful killing of a person. In verses 18–21 the Hebrew joins each command to the one before it with “and,” which Exodus 20 does not.
Hebrew shawʾ, “empty” or “worthless”; Exodus 20:16 has sheqer, “false.”

Exodus 20:17 puts the neighbor’s house first and uses the same verb, “covet” (Hebrew hamad), for both clauses. Here the wife comes first, a second verb (hitʾawweh, “crave” or “desire”) is used for the house and property, and “his field” is added. The Septuagint also has “his field.”
Hebrew “who of all flesh,” that is, what mortal.

verses.text: “Now this is the command—the statutes and the rulings—that Yahweh your God directed me to teach you, for you to carry out in the land you are crossing over to possess,
so that all your life you may revere Yahweh your God and observe all his statutes and commandments, which I am giving you—you, your son, and your grandson—in order that you may live long.
Listen, then, Israel, and take care to obey, so that you may prosper and become very numerous in a land flowing with milk and honey, just as Yahweh, the God of your forefathers, has promised you.{a}
“Hear,{b} Israel: Yahweh is our God; Yahweh is one.{c}
You shall love Yahweh your God with all your heart,{d} with all your soul,{e} and with all your strength.{f}
These words that I am commanding you today are to stay on your heart.
Impress them on your children. Talk about them when you are sitting at home and when you are out on the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
Bind them as a sign on your hand, and let them be a headband{g} between your eyes.
Inscribe them on the doorframes{h} of your house and on your city gates.

“Yahweh your God will bring you into the land that he swore to give you when he made his oath to your forefathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—a land with great and splendid cities that you did not build,
houses packed with all kinds of good things that you did not put there, cisterns you never dug, vineyards and olive trees you never planted. When you have eaten your fill,
be on your guard so that you do not forget Yahweh, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
Fear Yahweh your God, serve him, and take your oaths in his name.
Do not go after other gods, gods of the peoples who are all around you,
for Yahweh your God, who is in your midst, is a jealous God. Otherwise the anger of Yahweh your God will flare up against you, and he will sweep you off the face of the ground.
Do not test Yahweh your God the way you tested him at Massah.{i}
Be sure to keep the commands of Yahweh your God, and the testimonies and statutes he has laid on you.
Do what is upright and good in Yahweh’s sight, so that things may go well for you, and so that you may enter and take over the good land that Yahweh promised on oath to your forefathers,
by pushing all your enemies out of your way, as Yahweh has said.
“In days to come, when your son asks you, ‘What is the meaning of the testimonies, the statutes, and the rulings that Yahweh our God has commanded you?’
tell your son, ‘Pharaoh made slaves of us in Egypt, and Yahweh brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand.
Yahweh did signs and wonders, great and terrible, against Egypt, against Pharaoh, and against his entire household, while we watched.
But us he brought out from there, so that he might bring us in and give us the land that he had sworn to our forefathers.
Yahweh commanded us to perform all these statutes and to fear Yahweh our God, for our own good at all times, so that he might keep us alive, as he has to this day.
And it will count as righteousness for us if we take care to keep this whole command in the presence of Yahweh our God, as he has commanded us.’

notes.text: The Septuagint adds at the end of the verse, “and these are the ordinances and the judgments which the Lord commanded the children of Israel in the wilderness, when they had gone forth from the land of Egypt” (Brenton). The Nash Papyrus (see 5:6) is reported to have a similar heading before the Shema.

Hebrew shemaʿ, “hear” or “listen and obey.” From this word, verses 4–9 are known in Jewish tradition as the Shema. In many Hebrew manuscripts the last letter of “Hear” and the last letter of “one” are written large.

Or “Yahweh our God, Yahweh is one,” or “Yahweh our God is one Yahweh,” or “Yahweh is our God, Yahweh alone.” The Hebrew has four words after “Israel,” literally “Yahweh our-God Yahweh one,” with no verb. “One” may stress that Yahweh is undivided and unique, or that Israel is to worship Yahweh alone. The Septuagint reads “The Lord our God is one Lord,” the form quoted in Mark 12:29. The Nash Papyrus (see 5:6) contains this verse; it is reported to differ slightly from the Hebrew text used here.
Hebrew lebab, the center of thought, will, and feeling. The Septuagint has “mind.”
Or “your whole being” or “your life.”
Hebrew meʾod, literally “muchness,” that is, all your power and resources.
Hebrew totaphot, a word of uncertain meaning. Later Jewish practice understood this verse to refer to tefillin, small boxes containing these words, worn on the arm and forehead.
Hebrew mezuzot, from which comes the name mezuzah for the small case with these words fixed to a doorpost.
Massah means “testing” (Exodus 17:7).

verses.text: “When Yahweh your God brings you into the land you are entering to possess, he will clear away many nations ahead of you—the Hittite and the Girgashite, the Amorite and the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, seven nations more numerous and powerful than you.
When Yahweh your God hands them over to you and you strike them down, you must devote them to destruction. Make no covenant with them, and do not be merciful to them.
Do not marry among them. Do not give your daughter to his son, and do not take his daughter for your son,
because he would lead your son away from following me, and they would serve other gods. Then Yahweh’s anger would blaze against you, and he would destroy you quickly.
Rather, this is what you are to do to them: pull down their altars, shatter their standing stones, hack down their Asherah poles,{a} and burn their carved images.
For you are a people holy to Yahweh your God. Out of all the peoples on the face of the earth, Yahweh your God has chosen you to be a people that is his treasured possession.
Yahweh did not become attached to you and select you because your numbers exceeded those of the other peoples—indeed you were the smallest of all peoples—

It was because Yahweh loved you, and because he was keeping the oath he had sworn to your forefathers, that Yahweh brought you out with a strong hand and ransomed you from the house of slavery, out of the grip of Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
Know therefore that Yahweh your God, he is God, the faithful God, keeping covenant and loyal love to a thousand generations of those who love him and keep his commandments,
and who pays back those who hate him to their faces, destroying them. With the one who hates him he will not delay; he will pay him back to his face.
So keep the command, the statutes, and the rulings that I am giving you today, and carry them out.
“Because you listen to these rulings and keep them and act on them, Yahweh your God will keep with you the covenant and the steadfast love he swore to your forefathers.

and he will love you, bless you, and multiply you; he will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground, your grain, your new wine, and your oil, the increase of your herd and the young of your flock, in the land that he swore to your ancestors to give you.
You will be blessed beyond every other people. No man or woman among you will be childless, and none of your livestock will be barren.
Yahweh will turn every sickness away from you. He will not bring on you any of the dreadful diseases of Egypt that you know about; he will put them on all who hate you instead.
And you shall consume all the peoples whom Yahweh your God is giving over to you; your eye shall not spare them, nor shall you serve their gods, for that will be a snare to you.
“You may think to yourself, ‘These nations outnumber me. How can I drive them out?’
But do not be afraid of them. Call to mind what Yahweh your God did to Pharaoh and all Egypt:

the great ordeals your eyes witnessed, the signs and the wonders, the strong hand and the outstretched arm by which Yahweh your God brought you out. Yahweh your God will do just the same to all the peoples you are afraid of.
Yahweh your God will also send the hornet{b} against them, until even the survivors who hide from you have perished.
Do not tremble before them, for Yahweh your God is in your midst, a God great and awe-inspiring.
Yahweh your God will clear these nations away before you a little at a time. You will not be allowed to finish them off all at once, or the wild beasts would become too many for you.
Yahweh your God will deliver them up to you and throw them into great panic until they are wiped out.
He will hand their kings over to you, and you will blot out their names from under the heavens. No one will be able to hold his ground against you until you have destroyed them.

You shall burn the images of their gods in the fire. Do not desire the silver and the gold that covers them, and do not take it for yourself, or it will be a trap for you, for it is an abomination{c} to Yahweh your God.
Do not bring an abomination into your house, or you will become devoted to destruction as it is. You must regard it as vile and detest it, for it is devoted to destruction.

notes.text: Wooden poles or trees associated with the goddess Asherah.
Or “panic” or “plague”; the meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain. The Septuagint has “hornets.”
Hebrew toʿebah, something detestable or abhorrent, especially in worship.

verses.text: “Every command that I give you today you must take care to carry out, so that you may live and grow numerous and go in and possess the land Yahweh swore to your forefathers.

And remember the entire journey on which Yahweh your God has led you for forty years in the wilderness, to humble you, putting you to the test in order to learn what was in your heart, whether or not you would observe his commandments.

He humbled you, let you go hungry, and then fed you with manna,{a} which neither you nor your forefathers had ever known, so that he might teach you that people do not live on bread alone; rather, people live on every word that comes from Yahweh’s mouth.
Your clothes did not wear out on your backs, and your feet did not swell, all these forty years.
Know then in your heart that Yahweh your God disciplines you just as a man disciplines his son.
Keep the commands of Yahweh your God, walking in his ways and fearing him.
For Yahweh your God is bringing you into a good land, a land of flowing streams, of springs and underground waters that well up in the valleys and in the hills,
a land of wheat and barley, of vines and figs and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey,{b}
a land where you will never be short of bread to eat and will lack nothing, a land whose rocks contain iron and from whose hills you can mine copper.
You will eat until you are full, and you will bless Yahweh your God for the good land he has given you.
“Be careful not to forget Yahweh your God by neglecting his commands, his rulings, and his statutes, which I am commanding you today.
When you have eaten all you want and have built good houses and are living in them,
when your cattle and sheep have multiplied, your silver and gold have increased, and all that you own has grown,
do not let your heart become proud so that you forget Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
He led you through the vast and dreadful wilderness, a land of burning{c} serpents and scorpions, of parched ground with no water. He brought water out of hard rock for you.
He fed you manna in the wilderness, something your forefathers had never known, to humble you and put you to the test, so that in the end he might do you good.
Do not say to yourself, ‘My own strength and the power of my own hand have won me this wealth.’
Remember Yahweh your God, for it is he who gives you the power to gain wealth, so that he may establish his covenant that he swore to your forefathers, as he is doing today.
But if you do forget Yahweh your God and follow other gods and serve them and bow down to them, I warn you solemnly today that you will certainly perish.
Like the nations that Yahweh is wiping out before you, so you too will perish, because you would not obey the voice of Yahweh your God.

notes.text: Manna is probably named from the question “What is it?” (Exodus 16:15).
Probably both bees’ honey and the thick syrup made from dates or grapes.
Hebrew saraph, “burning,” perhaps from the painful bite of these snakes (Numbers 21:6).

verses.text: “Hear, Israel: today you are about to cross the Jordan to go in and dispossess nations bigger and mightier than you, with huge cities walled up to the sky,
a people great and tall, the sons of the Anakim, whom you know about, and about whom you have heard it said, ‘Who can make a stand against the sons of Anak?’

Know for certain today that it is Yahweh your God who will cross over in front of you, a consuming fire. He will destroy them; he will bring them down before you, and you will drive them out and make them vanish quickly, as Yahweh has told you.

When Yahweh your God has thrust them out of your way, do not say to yourself, ‘Yahweh brought me in to take this land because I am righteous.’ No, it is because these nations are wicked that Yahweh is driving them out before you.

You are not going in to take their land because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart. It is because of the wickedness of these nations that Yahweh your God is driving them out before you, and to keep the promise Yahweh swore to your forefathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Understand, then, that Yahweh your God is not giving you this good land to possess because of any righteousness of yours, for you are a stiff-necked people.
“Remember, and do not ever forget, how you made Yahweh your God angry in the wilderness. From the day you left the land of Egypt until you reached this place, you have been defying Yahweh.
At Horeb too you stirred Yahweh to anger, and his anger against you was enough to make him destroy you.

I had gone up the mountain to receive the stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant Yahweh had made with you, and I remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights without eating bread or drinking water.

Yahweh handed me the two stone tablets, written with the finger of God, and on them were all the words Yahweh had said to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire, on the day the people were assembled.
It was at the end of the forty days and forty nights that Yahweh gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.

Then Yahweh said to me, ‘Get up, go down from here at once, for the people you brought out of Egypt have behaved wickedly; they have been quick to leave the path I commanded them, and have made for themselves a cast image.’
Yahweh said further to me, ‘I have watched this people, and see what a stiff-necked people they are!
Let me be, so that I may destroy them and wipe their name out from under the heavens. Then I will make you into a nation stronger and larger than they are.’
So I turned and came down from the mountain, and the mountain was burning with fire, and the two tablets of the covenant were in my two hands.
When I looked, there you were: you had sinned against Yahweh your God. You had made yourselves a calf of cast metal. How quickly you had left the way Yahweh had commanded you!
So I grasped the two tablets, flung them down out of my hands, and smashed them before your eyes.

Then, as before, I lay face down before Yahweh forty days and forty nights, eating no bread and drinking no water, on account of every sin you had committed in doing what was evil in Yahweh’s sight and provoking him to anger.
For I dreaded the fury and wrath that Yahweh had turned against you, ready to destroy you. But again Yahweh listened to me that time.
With Aaron{a} too Yahweh was angry enough to destroy him, so I prayed for Aaron also at that time.

As for that sinful thing you had made, the calf, I took it and burned it up. I beat it to pieces and ground it down until it was fine as dust, and I threw the dust into the brook that runs down the mountain.
“At Taberah,{b} at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah{c} you angered Yahweh again.

And when Yahweh sent you out from Kadesh-barnea with the words, ‘Go up and possess the land I have given you,’ you defied the command of Yahweh your God. You put no trust in him and did not listen to his voice.
You have been rebels against Yahweh ever since I have known you.{d}
“So I lay face down before Yahweh for those forty days and forty nights, because Yahweh had said he would destroy you.
I prayed to Yahweh: ‘Lord Yahweh, do not destroy your people, your own inheritance, whom you ransomed by your greatness and brought out of Egypt with a strong hand.
Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Pay no attention to how stubborn this people is, to their wickedness or their sin,

lest the land from which you brought us out say, “Because Yahweh was not able to bring them into the land that he had promised them, and because he hated them, he has brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.”
But they are your own people and your inheritance, brought out by your great power and your outstretched arm.’

notes.text: The meaning of Aaron’s name is uncertain; it may be of Egyptian origin.
Taberah means “burning” (Numbers 11:1–3).
Kibroth-hattaavah means “graves of craving” (Numbers 11:34).
So the Hebrew. The Septuagint reads “from the day in which he became known to you” (Brenton), and the Samaritan Pentateuch is reported to have a similar reading.

verses.text: “At that time Yahweh said to me, ‘Carve out two stone tablets like the first pair and climb up to me on the mountain. Make yourself a wooden chest{a} too.
I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you smashed, and you are to place them in the chest.’
So I made a chest of acacia wood and carved two stone tablets like the first ones, and I went up the mountain holding the two tablets.
He wrote on the tablets, as he had written the first time, the Ten Words that Yahweh had spoken to you on the mountain out of the fire on the day of the assembly, and Yahweh gave them to me.
Then I turned, went back down the mountain, and put the tablets in the chest I had made. There they have remained, as Yahweh commanded me.
(The Israelites traveled from Beeroth Bene-jaakan{b} to Moserah.{c} Aaron died there and was buried there, and his son Eleazar{d} became priest in his place.
From there they traveled to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land with streams of running water.{e}
At that time Yahweh set the tribe of Levi{f} apart to carry the ark of Yahweh’s covenant, to stand in Yahweh’s presence and minister to him, and to bless in his name, which they do to this day.
This is why Levi has no portion or inheritance among his brothers. Yahweh himself is his inheritance, just as Yahweh your God told him.)
“I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights, as I had the first time. And Yahweh listened to me that time too; Yahweh chose not to destroy you.
Yahweh told me, ‘Get up and lead the people on their journey, so that they may go in and take possession of the land I swore to their forefathers to give them.’
“So now, Israel, what does Yahweh your God require of you? Only this: to fear Yahweh your God, to walk in all his ways and love him, to serve Yahweh your God with all your heart and all your soul,
and to keep the commands and statutes of Yahweh that I give you today, for your own good.
Look: to Yahweh your God belong the heavens, even the highest heavens, and the earth with all that is in it.
Yet Yahweh took delight in your forefathers and loved them, and he chose you, their descendants after them, from all the peoples, as you see today.
So circumcise your hearts,{g} and stop being stubborn.
For Yahweh your God is God over all gods and Lord over all lords, the great God, mighty and awe-inspiring, who plays no favorites and takes no bribes.
He upholds the cause of the fatherless and the widow, and he loves the foreigner, providing him with food and clothing.
You also must love the foreigner, for you were once foreigners in the land of Egypt.
Fear Yahweh your God and serve him. Hold fast to him, and swear your oaths by his name.
He is the one you praise; he is your God, who has done for you these great and fearsome things that you have seen with your own eyes.
When your forefathers went down to Egypt, they were seventy persons, and now Yahweh your God has made you as numerous as the stars of the sky.

notes.text: Hebrew ʾaron, “chest,” the word used for the ark of the covenant (verse 8).
Beeroth Bene-jaakan means “wells of the sons of Jaakan.” The Septuagint reads “Beeroth of the sons of Jakim.”
Moserah may mean “chastening.” Numbers 33:30–38 lists these stopping places in a different order and places Aaron’s death at Mount Hor.
Eleazar means “God has helped.”
Gudgodah may mean “cleft”; Jotbathah means “pleasantness.” The Septuagint spells them Gadgad and Etebatha.
Levi probably means “joined” or “attached” (Genesis 29:34).
Hebrew “circumcise the foreskin of your hearts.”

verses.text: “Love Yahweh your God, and always keep what he requires: his statutes, his rulings, and his commands.
Consider today—for it is not your children I am speaking to, who have not known or seen it—the discipline of Yahweh your God, his greatness, his mighty hand and outstretched arm,
the signs and the deeds he performed in Egypt against Pharaoh king of Egypt and his whole country,
and what he did to the Egyptian army, its horses and chariots, in making the waters of the Red Sea flow over them while they were chasing you, so that Yahweh annihilated them to this very day;
what he did for you in the wilderness until you arrived here,

and what he did to Dathan and Abiram,{a} the sons of Eliab the son of Reuben, how the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their households, their tents, and every living being in their possession, in the midst of all Israel.
Your own eyes have seen every great deed that Yahweh has done.
“So keep every command I give you today, so that you will be strong enough to enter and take the land you are crossing over to possess,
and so that you may live long in the land Yahweh swore to give to your forefathers and to their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey.
For the land you are about to enter and possess is unlike the land of Egypt, which you left, where you would sow your seed and water it by foot,{b} as in a vegetable garden.
But the land you are going over to take is a land of hills and valleys, which drinks water from the rain of heaven,
a land Yahweh your God looks after. The eyes of Yahweh your God are always on it, from the start of the year to its close.
“And if you indeed listen to my commandments that I command you today, to love Yahweh your God and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul,
then I{c} will send rain on your land at the proper time, the autumn rain and the spring rain,{d} and you will gather in your grain, your new wine, and your oil.
I will make grass grow in your fields for your livestock, and you will eat your fill.
Be on your guard, so that your hearts are not led astray and you turn away to serve other gods and worship them.
Then Yahweh’s anger would burn against you. He would close up the sky so that no rain falls and the soil gives no harvest, and you would soon disappear from the good land Yahweh is giving you.
“Store up these words of mine in your heart and soul. Tie them as a sign on your hand, and let them be a headband between your eyes.
Teach them to your children, talking about them as you sit at home and as you travel the road, as you lie down and as you rise.
Write them on the doorframes of your house and on your gates,
so that you and your children may live many days in the land Yahweh swore to your forefathers to give them, as long as the heavens stand above the earth.
For if you will diligently observe this entire commandment which I am giving you to perform—to love Yahweh your God, to walk in all his ways, and to cling to him—
then Yahweh will drive out all these nations from before you, and you will dispossess nations greater and mightier than yourselves.
Every place your foot steps on will be yours. Your borders will run from the wilderness to Lebanon, and from the River—the Euphrates—to the western sea.{e}
No one will be able to stand against you; Yahweh your God will put the dread and fear of you on all the land on which you tread, just as he told you.
“Look: today I am placing before you blessing and curse:
a blessing if you obey the commands of Yahweh your God that I am giving you today,
and a curse if you disobey the commands of Yahweh your God and leave the way I am commanding you today by following other gods you have not known.
When Yahweh your God has brought you into the land you are going to possess, you are to proclaim the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.{f}
These mountains are across the Jordan, are they not, west of the road where the sun sets, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, near Gilgal, beside the great trees{g} of Moreh.{h}
For you are about to cross the Jordan to go in and take the land Yahweh your God is giving you. When you have taken it and are living in it,
be careful to carry out all the statutes and rulings I am setting before you today.

notes.text: Dathan may mean “belonging to a fountain” (uncertain); Abiram means “my father is exalted”; Eliab means “my God is father”; Reuben means “See, a son!” (Genesis 29:32). See Numbers 16.
Probably by opening and closing small irrigation channels with the foot, or by treading a water wheel.
So the Hebrew; the Septuagint has “he will give,” and other ancient witnesses are reported to agree.
Hebrew “the early rain and the late rain”: the autumn rains that soften the ground for plowing (about October–November) and the spring rains that fill out the grain (about March–April).
Hebrew “the sea behind,” the Mediterranean; the Hebrew compass faced east.
Gerizim and Ebal stand on either side of Shechem; the meanings of their names are uncertain. See 27:11–13.
Or “oaks” or “terebinths.” The Septuagint has the singular, “by the high oak” (Brenton).
Moreh means “teacher.” Gilgal means “circle,” perhaps of stones.

verses.text: “These are the statutes and ordinances that you shall be careful to observe in the land that Yahweh, the God of your ancestors, has given you to possess, as long as you live upon the earth.
Utterly destroy every place where the nations you are dispossessing served their gods, on the lofty mountains, on the hills, and beneath every green tree.
Tear down their altars, shatter their standing stones, burn their Asherah poles, cut to pieces the carved images of their gods, and erase their names from that place.
You must not worship Yahweh your God in the way they worship.
Instead, you shall seek the place that Yahweh your God will choose out of all your tribes to set his name there as his dwelling,{a} and there you shall go.

There you are to bring your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contributions of your hand,{b} your vowed offerings and your freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your cattle and your flocks.
There, in the presence of Yahweh your God, you and your households shall eat and be glad in all that you have set your hand to, because Yahweh your God has blessed you.
“You must not act as we are acting here today, where everyone does whatever he himself thinks right,
for you have not yet reached the rest and the inheritance that Yahweh your God is giving you.
But when you cross the Jordan and live in the land that Yahweh your God is giving you as an inheritance, and he gives you rest from all your enemies around you, so that you live in safety,

Then, to the place that Yahweh your God chooses for his name to dwell, you shall bring all that I command you: your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contributions of your hand, and all your finest vowed offerings that you vow to Yahweh.

There you shall rejoice before Yahweh your God, along with your sons and daughters and the slaves who serve you, men and women, and with the Levite who lives inside your gates, since no share or inheritance of land has been given him among you.
Be careful not to offer up your burnt offerings in just any place you see.
Only in the place that Yahweh chooses within one of your tribes shall you offer your burnt offerings, and there you shall do all that I command you.

“Nevertheless, whenever you wish, you may slaughter animals and eat meat in any of your towns, according to the blessing that Yahweh your God has given you. Both the unclean and the clean may eat of it, just as they eat gazelle or deer.
Only the blood you are not to eat; let it run out onto the ground like water.

Within your towns you may not eat the tithe of your grain, your new wine, or your oil, nor the firstborn of your cattle or your flock, nor any of your vowed offerings that you vow, your freewill offerings, or the contributions of your hand.

Instead, you shall eat these before Yahweh your God in the place Yahweh your God chooses—you and your children, the slaves who serve you, men and women, and the Levite in your towns—and you shall rejoice before Yahweh your God in every task you undertake.
Take care never to abandon the Levite, for as long as you live on your land.
“When Yahweh your God widens your borders, as he has promised you, and you say, ‘I want to eat meat,’ because you long for meat, then eat meat whenever you like.

If the place where Yahweh your God chooses to put his name is far away from you, you may slaughter animals from the cattle and sheep Yahweh has given you, in the way I have commanded you, and you may eat them in your own towns whenever you wish.
You may eat it just as gazelle or deer is eaten; both the unclean and the clean may eat of it.
But hold firm: the blood is not to be eaten, for the blood is the life, and the life must not be eaten together with the flesh.
Do not eat it; pour it out on the ground like water.
Do not eat it, so that things may go well for you and for your children after you, as you do what is right in Yahweh’s sight.
But the holy offerings that are due from you, and your vowed offerings, you shall take with you to the place Yahweh chooses.

Present your burnt offerings, both the flesh and the blood, on the altar of Yahweh your God. As for your other sacrifices, their blood is poured out at the side of the altar of Yahweh your God, while the flesh you may eat.

Listen to all these words I am commanding you and keep them, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you for all time, as you do what is good and right in the sight of Yahweh your God.
“When Yahweh your God has cut off before you the nations whose land you are entering to take, and you have dispossessed them and are living in their land,

take care that you are not lured into following their ways once they have been wiped out before you. Do not go asking about their gods, ‘In what way did these nations serve their gods? I will copy them.’
You must not do that for Yahweh your God, for they have done for their gods every detestable thing that Yahweh hates. They even burn their sons and daughters in the fire as offerings to their gods.
“Whatever I command you, be careful to do it. You must neither add to it nor subtract from it.{c}

notes.text: Or “to put his name there, to make it dwell.” The Hebrew can be read either way.
Hebrew terumah, a portion “lifted” or set apart from one’s goods as an offering.
Verse 32 is 13:1 in the Hebrew text.

verses.text: “Suppose a prophet or someone who has dreams appears among you and announces to you a sign or a wonder,{a}
and the sign or wonder he told you about takes place, and he says, ‘Let us follow other gods’—gods you have not known—‘and let us serve them.’

You must not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer of dreams, for Yahweh your God is testing you, to find out whether you love Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
It is Yahweh your God whom you must follow, and him you must fear. Keep his commands and listen to his voice; serve him and cling to him.

As for that prophet or dreamer of dreams, he is to be put to death, for he preached revolt against Yahweh your God, who brought you out of Egypt’s land and ransomed you from the house of slavery, trying to lead you away from the path Yahweh your God commanded you to follow. In this way you shall cleanse out the evil from among you.

“Suppose your brother, the son of your own mother, or your son or your daughter, or the wife you hold in your arms, or the friend who is like your own self, secretly tries to entice you, saying, ‘Come, let us go and serve other gods’—gods that neither you nor your forefathers have known,
gods of the surrounding peoples, whether they live close by or far off, from one edge of the earth to the other—
do not yield to him or listen to him. Have no pity on him; do not spare him or cover for him.
Instead, you must surely kill him. Your own hand must be the first raised against him to put him to death, and after that the hands of all the people.
Stone him with stones until he dies, because he tried to turn you away from Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
Then all Israel will hear of it and fear, and never again will anyone among you do such wickedness.
“Suppose you hear that in one of the towns Yahweh your God is giving you to live in,
some worthless men{b} have come out from among you and have led astray the people of their town, saying, ‘Let us go and serve other gods,’ gods you have not known.
Then you must investigate, examine, and inquire carefully. If the report proves true and the thing is established, that this abominable deed has been committed in your midst,
you must put the people of that town to the sword, devoting it to destruction with all that is in it, its cattle included, by the sword.

Gather all its plunder into the middle of the town square, and burn the town and all its plunder in the fire as a whole offering{c} to Yahweh your God. It shall remain a heap of ruins forever and never be built again.

Nothing from the devoted things shall stick to your hand, in order that Yahweh may turn from the fierceness of his anger and grant you mercy, and have compassion on you and multiply you, as he swore to your ancestors,
because you listen to the voice of Yahweh your God, keeping all his commands that I give you today, and doing what is right in the sight of Yahweh your God.

notes.text: Verses 1–18 are numbered 2–19 in the Hebrew text.
Hebrew “sons of Belial,” an expression of uncertain origin for worthless or wicked people.
Hebrew kalil, “complete,” a word used for an offering that is entirely burned.

verses.text: “You are the children of Yahweh your God. You must not gash yourselves or make yourselves bald on your foreheads{a} on account of the dead,
for you are a people holy to Yahweh your God. Yahweh has chosen you out of all the peoples on the face of the earth to be his own people, his treasured possession.
“Do not eat anything abominable.
These are the animals you may eat: cattle, sheep, and goats,
the deer, the gazelle, the roebuck, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope, and the mountain sheep.{b}
Any animal that has a split hoof, divided into two parts, and that chews the cud, among the animals, you may eat.

However, among those that chew the cud or have a divided and split hoof, you must not eat these: the camel, the hare, and the rock badger.{c} They chew the cud, yet their hoof is not split; they are unclean for you.
And the pig, because it has a split hoof but does not chew the cud, is unclean for you. You must not eat their flesh or touch their dead bodies.
“Among all the creatures living in the water, these you may eat: any with fins and scales may be eaten.
But whatever does not have fins and scales you must not eat; it is unclean for you.
“Every clean bird you may eat.
These, however, you must not eat: the eagle,{d} the bearded vulture, and the black vulture,
the red kite, the falcon, and every kind of kite,{e}
every kind of raven,
the ostrich, the nighthawk, the gull, and every kind of hawk,
the little owl, the great owl, the white owl,
the pelican, the carrion vulture, the cormorant,
the stork, every kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
Every winged insect that swarms is unclean for you; it must not be eaten.
You may eat any clean winged creature.

“You shall not eat any carcass; you may give it to the resident alien in your gates, that he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner; for you are a holy people to Yahweh your God. You shall not cook a kid in its mother’s milk.
“Be sure to give a tenth of all the yield of your seed, which the field produces year by year.

Before Yahweh your God, in the place where he chooses to settle his name, you are to eat the tithe of your grain, your new wine, and your oil, along with the firstborn of your herds and flocks, that you may learn always to revere Yahweh your God.

But if the distance is too great for you, so that you cannot carry the tithe, because the place where Yahweh your God chooses to put his name is too far from you, when Yahweh your God has blessed you,
then exchange it for silver. Tie up the silver, take it in your hand, and go to the place Yahweh your God chooses.
Spend the silver on anything you wish: cattle, sheep, wine, beer, or whatever you desire. Then eat there in the presence of Yahweh your God and celebrate, you and your household together.
And as for the Levite who lives in your towns, do not abandon him, for he has no portion or inheritance of his own among you.
“At the end of every third year, bring out the whole tithe of your harvest for that year and store it up in your towns.

And the Levite, because he has no portion or inheritance with you, and the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow in your towns, shall come and eat and be satisfied, that Yahweh your God may bless you in all the work of your hand that you do.

notes.text: Hebrew “make a baldness between your eyes.”
The identification of several of the animals in this verse is uncertain.
Hebrew shaphan, the rock hyrax.
Or “griffon vulture.” Many of the birds in verses 12–18 cannot be identified with certainty.
Hebrew lists three birds here, the second and third written with similar letters; Leviticus 11:14 has only two, and the Septuagint and other ancient witnesses are reported to differ in this list.

verses.text: “At the end of every seven years you shall grant a release.{a}

This is the manner of the release: every creditor is to let go of the claim on what he has lent to his neighbor. He must not demand repayment from his neighbor, his brother, because a release has been proclaimed in Yahweh’s honor.
You may demand payment from a foreigner, but whatever is owed to you by your brother you must let go.
There should, however, be no one in need among you, because Yahweh will surely bless you in the land Yahweh your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess,
if only you will listen closely to the voice of Yahweh your God and take care to keep this whole command that I am giving you today.
For Yahweh your God will bless you as he promised; you will make loans to many nations without borrowing, and you will govern many nations while none governs you.
“If anyone among you is in need, one of your brothers, in any town of the land Yahweh your God is giving you, do not harden your heart against your poor brother or close your hand to him.
Instead, open your hand to him generously, and willingly lend him enough to meet his need, whatever he lacks.

Watch out that no base thought enters your heart, such as, ‘The seventh year, the year of release, is drawing near,’ so that you look on your needy brother with a grudging eye and give him nothing. He may then cry out to Yahweh against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
Give to him freely, and do not give with a grudging heart, because for this Yahweh your God will bless you in all your work and in everything you put your hand to.
The poor will never disappear from the land. That is why I command you to open your hand freely to your brother, to the poor and needy in your land.
“If one of your own people, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, is sold to you and serves you six years, in the seventh year you must set him free.
And when you set him free, you must not send him off with nothing.
Load him generously with gifts from your flock, your threshing floor, and your winepress. Give to him in the measure that Yahweh your God has blessed you.
Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt and that Yahweh your God ransomed you. That is why I am giving you this command today.
But if he tells you, ‘I do not want to leave you,’ because he loves you and your household and is content with you,
then take an awl and push it through his ear into the door, and he will be your servant for good. You shall treat your female slave the same way.
Do not think it hard to set him free, because his six years of service to you have been worth twice the wages of a hired worker. And Yahweh your God will bless you in everything you do.
“You must set apart for Yahweh your God every firstborn male of your cattle and your flock. Do not put the firstborn of your cattle to work, and do not shear the firstborn of your sheep.
Year by year you and your household shall eat them in the presence of Yahweh your God, at the place Yahweh chooses.
But if an animal has a defect—if it is lame or blind, or has any serious blemish—it is not to be sacrificed to Yahweh your God.
You may eat it in your own towns; the unclean and the clean alike may eat it, as they would a gazelle or a deer.
Only you must not eat its blood; pour it out on the ground like water.

notes.text: Hebrew shemittah, a “letting drop,” here the cancellation or suspension of debts.

verses.text: “Observe the month of Abib (March–April){a} and keep the Passover for Yahweh your God, for in the month of Abib Yahweh your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
You shall sacrifice the Passover animal to Yahweh your God from the flock or the herd, at the place where Yahweh chooses to make his name dwell.

You are not to eat anything leavened with it. For seven days eat unleavened bread along with it, the bread of affliction—since you left the land of Egypt in haste—so that you will recall, as long as you live, the day of your departure from the land of Egypt.
For seven days no leaven is to be found anywhere in your territory, and none of the meat you sacrifice in the evening on the first day is to be left over until morning.
You are not allowed to sacrifice the Passover inside any one of the towns Yahweh your God is giving you,
Only at the place where Yahweh your God chooses to make his name dwell shall you sacrifice the Passover, in the evening as the sun goes down,{b} at the time of day you came out of Egypt.
You shall cook it and eat it at the place Yahweh your God chooses, and in the morning you may turn back and go home to your tents.
For six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and the seventh day shall be a solemn assembly for Yahweh your God. You shall do no work on it.
“Count off seven weeks, starting from the day you first put the sickle to the standing grain.
Then celebrate the Feast of Weeks{c} to Yahweh your God by bringing a freewill offering from your hand, giving in proportion to the way Yahweh your God has blessed you.

And you shall rejoice in the presence of Yahweh your God, at the place he chooses to settle his name: you and your son and daughter, your male and female servants, the Levite in your gates, and the sojourner, the orphan, and the widow in your midst.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and take care to keep these statutes.
“You shall celebrate the Feast of Booths{d} for seven days, after you have gathered in the yield of your threshing floor and your winepress.
You shall rejoice at your feast—you, your son and daughter, your male and female servants, and the Levite, the sojourner, the orphan, and the widow who live in your gates.
For seven days you shall hold the feast for Yahweh your God at the site Yahweh selects; for Yahweh your God will bless all your harvest and every work of your hands, and your joy will be complete.

Three times a year all your males are to appear before Yahweh your God at the place he chooses: at the Feast of Unleavened Bread, at the Feast of Weeks, and at the Feast of Booths. No one is to appear before Yahweh with empty hands.
Each of you shall bring a gift in keeping with what he can give, according to the blessing that Yahweh your God has given you.
