“You shall appoint judges and officials in all your towns that Yahweh your God is giving you, tribe by tribe, and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.
You must not pervert justice or show favoritism. Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of those who are in the right.
Pursue justice, nothing but justice, so that you may live and take possession of the land that Yahweh your God is giving you.
“Do not plant any kind of tree as an Asherah pole next to the altar you build for Yahweh your God,
and do not set up for yourself a sacred stone, which Yahweh your God hates.

notes.text: Hebrew “the month of Abib” (“ear of grain”), the month when the barley ripened, later called Nisan. It is the first month of the year counted from spring (Exodus 12:2; 13:4). The Hebrew calendar is lunar, so the modern equivalent is approximate.
Hebrew “in the evening, at the going down of the sun.” Exodus 12:6 has the Passover lamb slaughtered “between the two evenings,” that is, at twilight.
Hebrew Shavuot, later also called Pentecost, held seven weeks after Passover, in the third month, Sivan (May–June).
Or “Tabernacles” (Hebrew Sukkot), held in the seventh month, Tishri (September–October); see Leviticus 23:34.

verses.text: “You must not sacrifice to Yahweh your God an ox or a sheep that has a blemish or any defect at all, for that is detestable to Yahweh your God.
“Suppose there is found among you, in one of the towns Yahweh your God is giving you, a man or woman who does what is evil in the sight of Yahweh your God by breaking his covenant,
and has gone and served other gods and bowed down to them, or to the sun or the moon or any of the host of heaven, which I have forbidden,
and it is reported to you and you hear of it. Then you shall make a thorough inquiry, and if it is true and the fact is confirmed that this detestable act has been done in Israel,
you shall lead out to your town gates the man or the woman guilty of this wicked deed, and that man or woman shall be stoned until dead.
On the evidence of two witnesses or three witnesses the person who is to die shall be executed; he shall not be executed on the evidence of one witness.
The hands of the witnesses shall be the first raised against him to put him to death, and afterward the hands of all the people. So you shall burn away the evil from your midst.

“If any case arises in your towns that is too hard for you—a matter of bloodshed, of civil rights, or of assault, cases of dispute—then you shall arise and go up to the place that Yahweh your God chooses.
Go to the Levitical priests and to the judge who holds office in those days. Consult them, and they will declare to you the verdict.
Then you must act according to the decision they announce to you from that place that Yahweh chooses. Be careful to do exactly as they instruct you.
Act according to the instruction they teach you and the ruling they give you. Do not depart from the sentence they pronounce, either to the right or to the left.
Anyone who acts arrogantly and will not listen to the priest who stands there to minister before Yahweh your God, or to the judge, that man shall die. So you shall burn away the evil from Israel.
All the people will hear of it and be afraid, and they will not act presumptuously again.
“When you come into the land Yahweh your God is giving you and have made it yours and are living there, and you say, ‘Let me put a king over myself, like all the surrounding nations,’
you may indeed set over yourself a king whom Yahweh your God chooses. Set as king over you one from among your own brothers; you may not put a foreigner over you, one who is not your brother.
Only he must not acquire great numbers of horses for himself, or send the people back to Egypt to get more horses, since Yahweh has told you, ‘You shall never go back that way again.’
He must not take many wives for himself, or his heart will turn away, and he must not pile up for himself great amounts of silver and gold.
Once he is seated on his royal throne, he is to copy out for himself on a scroll this law,{a} from the text in the keeping of the Levitical priests.
It shall be with him, and he shall read in it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear Yahweh his God by keeping all the words of this law and these statutes and doing them,
so that he will not think himself above his fellow Israelites, nor turn from the commandment to right or left; then he and his descendants will have a long reign in Israel.

notes.text: The Septuagint renders “a copy of this law” as to deuteronomion touto, “this repetition of the law” (Brenton), literally “this second law,” from which the book’s English name, Deuteronomy, comes.

verses.text: “The Levitical priests, the whole tribe of Levi, shall have no share or inheritance with Israel. They shall live on the food offerings{a} made to Yahweh, which are his inheritance.
They shall have no inheritance among their brothers; Yahweh himself is their inheritance, as he promised them.
This shall be the priests’ due from the people who offer a sacrifice, whether an ox or a sheep: they shall give the priest the shoulder, the two cheeks, and the stomach.
You shall also give him the firstfruits of your grain, your new wine, and your oil, and the first fleece of your sheep.
For Yahweh your God has chosen him and his sons out of all your tribes to stand and minister in the name of Yahweh for all time.
“If a Levite comes from one of your towns anywhere in Israel where he has been living, and he comes with all the desire of his heart to the place Yahweh chooses,
then he may minister in the name of Yahweh his God like all his fellow Levites who stand there before Yahweh.
He shall receive an equal portion to eat, besides what he receives from the sale of his family’s possessions.{b}
“When you enter the land Yahweh your God is giving you, do not learn to copy the detestable practices of those nations.
Let no one be found among you who makes his son or daughter pass through the fire, or who practices divination, or tells fortunes, or reads omens, or is a sorcerer,
or casts spells, or consults ghosts or familiar spirits, or seeks answers from the dead.
Whoever does such things is detestable to Yahweh, and it is because of these detestable things that Yahweh your God is driving those nations out before you.
You must be blameless before Yahweh your God.
For these nations, which you are about to dispossess, listen to soothsayers and diviners; but as for you, Yahweh your God has not permitted you to do so.
“From your own midst, from among your brothers, Yahweh your God will raise up a prophet like me for you. To him you shall listen.
This is what you asked of Yahweh your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, when you said, ‘Let us not hear the voice of Yahweh our God again or see this great fire any more, or we will die.’
And Yahweh said to me, ‘They have spoken well.
From among their brothers I will raise up a prophet for them, one like you. My words I will place in his mouth, and he will speak to them all that I command him.
And anyone who refuses to listen to my words, which that prophet speaks in my name, I myself will hold accountable.
But the prophet who presumes to speak a word in my name that I have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods, that same prophet shall die.’
And if you say in your heart, ‘How can we tell which word Yahweh has not spoken?’—

If a prophet speaks in Yahweh’s name, and the word does not come about or come to pass, that is a word that Yahweh has not spoken; the prophet has spoken it presumptuously; you shall not be afraid of him.

notes.text: Hebrew ’isshe, offerings presented by fire or as food gifts; the exact sense is debated.
Hebrew obscure; literally “besides his sales according to the fathers.”

verses.text: “When Yahweh your God has cut off the nations whose land he is giving you, and you have driven them out and are living in their cities and houses,
you shall set apart three towns for yourselves in the land Yahweh your God is giving you to possess.
Prepare the roads, and divide into three parts the territory of the land that Yahweh your God is giving you as an inheritance, so that anyone who kills a person may flee there.
This is the rule for the one who kills someone and flees there to save his life: he must have struck his neighbor unintentionally, without having hated him in the past.

For example, a man goes into the forest with his neighbor to cut wood, and as he swings the axe to fell a tree, the head flies off the handle and strikes his neighbor so that he dies. That man may flee to one of these towns and live.

Otherwise the avenger of blood,{a} in hot anger, might pursue the killer and overtake him because the way is long, and strike him dead, though he did not deserve death, since he had not hated his neighbor in the past.
That is why I command you to set apart three towns for yourselves.
And if Yahweh your God enlarges your territory, as he swore to your forefathers, and gives you all the land he promised to give to your forefathers—
provided that you carefully observe this whole commandment that I am giving you today, loving Yahweh your God and walking in his ways at all times—then you shall add three more cities to these three.
so that innocent blood may not be shed in the land Yahweh your God is giving you as an inheritance, and so that bloodguilt may not be on you.
“But if a man hates his neighbor and lies in wait for him, attacks him, and strikes him a fatal blow so that he dies, and then flees to one of these towns,
the elders of his own town shall send for him, have him brought back from there, and deliver him into the hand of the blood avenger, and he shall die.
Show him no pity. You must purge the guilt of innocent blood from Israel, so that it may go well with you.
“Do not move your neighbor’s boundary marker, set up by those who came before you, in the inheritance you will receive in the land Yahweh your God is giving you to possess.
“A single witness shall not be enough to convict a person of any crime or offense that he may have committed. A matter shall be established only on the evidence of two witnesses or of three.
If a malicious witness rises up against someone to accuse him of wrongdoing,
then both parties to the dispute shall stand before Yahweh, before the priests and the judges who are in office in those days.
The judges shall investigate thoroughly, and if the witness turns out to be a false witness who has testified falsely against his brother,
then you shall do to him what he had intended to do to his brother. So you shall burn away the evil from your midst.
Those who remain will hear and fear, and no one will ever again commit such wickedness among you.
Show no pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

notes.text: Hebrew go’el haddam, the relative responsible for avenging a kinsman’s death.

verses.text: “When you go out to war against your enemies and see horses and chariots and an army larger than your own, do not be afraid of them; for Yahweh your God is with you, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.
As you approach the battle, the priest is to step forward and address the troops.
He shall say to them, ‘Hear, Israel: today you are drawing near to battle against your enemies. Do not lose heart. Do not be afraid, do not panic, and do not tremble before them,
for Yahweh your God is the one who goes with you to fight for you against your enemies and to save you.’
Then the officers shall say to the people: ‘Who is the man that has built a new house but has not yet inaugurated it? Let him return home, or he might die in the battle and another man inaugurate it.
And is there anyone who has planted a vineyard but has not yet enjoyed it? Let him go home, lest he die in battle and someone else enjoy it.
Has anyone become engaged to a woman and not yet married her? Let him go back to his house, or he may die in the battle and another man marry her.’
Then the officers shall say further to the people, ‘Is any man fearful and faint of heart? He should return home, lest his fellow soldiers lose courage as he has.’
When the officers have finished speaking to the people, commanders of the troops shall be appointed to lead them.
“When you draw near to a town to fight against it, first offer it terms of peace.
If it answers you peaceably and opens its gates to you, then all the people found in it shall serve you at forced labor.
But if it will not make peace with you but makes war against you, then you shall besiege it.
And when Yahweh your God delivers it into your hand, you shall put every male in it to the sword.

But the women, the children, the animals, and whatever else is in the town, all its plunder, you may seize for yourselves, and you may make use of what you take from your enemies, which Yahweh your God has given you.
That is the way to deal with all the cities far away from you, those that do not belong to the nations nearby.
But in the towns of these peoples that Yahweh your God is giving you as an inheritance, you must not leave alive anything that breathes.
You must devote them to complete destruction—the Hittite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite{a}—as Yahweh your God has commanded you,
so that they will not teach you to do all the detestable things they have done for their gods, and so cause you to sin against Yahweh your God.

“When you lay siege to a city for many days, fighting against it to take it, do not ruin its trees by putting an axe to them. Eat their fruit, but do not chop them down. Is the tree of the field a man, that it should come under siege from you?{b}
Only the trees you know do not bear fruit you may destroy and cut down, to build siegeworks against the town that is making war with you, until it falls.

notes.text: The Septuagint adds “and the Girgashite” (the Samaritan Pentateuch is reported to agree), making seven nations as in 7:1.
Or “for the tree of the field is man’s life.” The Hebrew is difficult.

verses.text: “Suppose a murdered body is discovered lying in a field in the land Yahweh your God is giving you to possess, and no one knows who struck him down.
Your elders and judges shall go out and measure from the body to each of the towns around it.
Then the elders of whichever town is closest to the body shall take a young cow that has never been put to work or drawn a load under a yoke.
and the elders of that town shall take the heifer to a wadi with flowing water, one that has not been tilled or sown, and there in the wadi they shall break the heifer’s neck.

Then the priests, the sons of Levi, shall come forward, for Yahweh your God has chosen them to serve him and to give blessings in Yahweh’s name, and every lawsuit and case of violence is to be decided by what they say.
All the elders of that town nearest the slain man shall wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley,
and they shall testify, ‘Our hands did not spill this blood, nor did our eyes see it happen.
Make atonement, Yahweh, for your people Israel, whom you have redeemed, and do not lay the guilt of innocent blood on your people Israel.’ Then the bloodguilt will be atoned for on their behalf.
In this way you will remove from among you the guilt of innocent blood, by doing what is upright in Yahweh’s eyes.
“When you march out to fight your enemies, and Yahweh your God hands them over to you and you carry off prisoners,
and you see among the captives a beautiful woman and desire her and take her as your wife,
then you shall bring her home to your house, and she shall shave her head and trim her nails.
and she shall remove her captive’s garments, and stay in your house and mourn her father and mother for a whole month; afterward you may go in to her and be her husband, and she shall be your wife.
And if you take no delight in her, you shall let her go where she pleases; but you shall by no means sell her for money, nor deal with her as a slave, because you have dishonored her.
“Suppose a man has two wives, one whom he loves and one whom he does not, and each of them has borne him sons, but the eldest son was born to the wife who is not loved.
then when he gives his sons their inheritance, he cannot make the son of the favored wife the firstborn ahead of the son of the disliked wife, who is the actual firstborn.

He must instead recognize the firstborn, the son of the disliked wife, by giving him a double share of everything he owns; for he is the first of his vigor, and the right of the firstborn belongs to him.
“If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who will not obey his father or his mother, and though they discipline him, he will not listen to them,
then his father and mother shall seize him and take him out to the elders of his city, to the gate of the place where he lives,
They shall tell the elders of the town, ‘Our son here is defiant and disobedient; he refuses to listen to us. He eats too much and drinks too much.’
Then all the men of his town shall stone him until he dies. In this way you will remove the evil from among you, and all Israel will hear of it and fear.
“If a man has committed a crime worthy of death and is put to death, and you hang him on a tree,

his corpse shall not hang overnight on the tree, but you shall bury it that same day, for a hanged man is accursed of God;{a} you shall not defile your land, which Yahweh your God is giving you as an inheritance.

notes.text: Or “an insult to God.” Galatians 3:13 quotes this verse in a form close to the Septuagint.

verses.text: “If you see your brother’s ox or his sheep straying, do not pretend you have not seen them. Be sure to bring them back to your brother.
If your brother does not live near you, or you do not know who he is, take the animal home with you and keep it until he comes looking for it; then give it back to him.
Do the same with his donkey, with his cloak, and with anything your brother loses and you find. You must not look the other way.
If you see your brother’s donkey or his ox fallen on the road, do not turn away from them. You must help him lift them up again.
“A woman shall not wear a man’s gear, and a man shall not put on a woman’s garment, for whoever does such things is detestable to Yahweh your God.

“If you come across a bird’s nest beside the road, in any tree or on the ground, with fledglings or eggs, and the mother is sitting on the fledglings or the eggs, you shall not take the mother with her young.
Let the mother go free, though you may take the young for yourself, so that things may go well with you and you may live long.
“When you build a new house, put a parapet around your roof, so that you do not bring bloodguilt on your house if anyone falls from it.
“You shall not sow your vineyard with two kinds of seed, lest the whole produce become forfeit,{a} both the seed you have sown and the yield of the vineyard.
Do not plow with an ox and a donkey yoked together.
Do not wear cloth woven of wool and linen mixed together.
“Make tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wrap around yourself.
“Suppose a man marries a woman and goes in to her, and then turns against her,
and charges her with shameful conduct and gives her a bad name, saying, ‘I married this woman, but when I came near her I found no proof of her virginity.’
Then the young woman’s father and mother shall bring out the proof of her virginity to the elders of the town at the gate.
Her father shall say to the elders, ‘I gave my daughter to this man as his wife, and he has turned against her.

Now he has accused her of shameful things, claiming, “Your daughter was not a virgin when I found her.” Yet here is the evidence that she was.’ Then they are to unfold the garment in front of the town’s elders.
The elders of the town are then to seize the man and discipline him.

They shall fine him 2½ pounds of silver{b} and give it to the young woman’s father, because he has given a bad name to a virgin of Israel. She shall remain his wife; he may never divorce her as long as he lives.
But if the accusation proves true, and the evidence that the girl was a virgin cannot be found,

then they shall bring her out to the door of her father’s house, and the men of her town shall stone her to death, because she has done a disgraceful thing in Israel by acting as a prostitute in her father’s house. So you shall burn away the evil from your midst.
“If a man is discovered in bed with another man’s wife, both shall die—the man who slept with the woman, and the woman. In this way you shall purge the evil from Israel.
“If there is a young woman who is a virgin, pledged to be married to a man, and another man meets her in the town and lies with her,

bring the two of them out to that town’s gate and stone them until they die—the girl because, though she was inside the town, she raised no cry, and the man because he dishonored the wife of his neighbor. So you shall burn away the evil from your midst.
But if it is out in the countryside that the man meets the engaged young woman, and he seizes her and lies with her, then only the man who lay with her shall die.
Do nothing to the girl, for there is no sin in her that deserves death. It is just as when a man rises against his neighbor and kills him.
For he met her in the open country, and though the engaged young woman cried out, there was no one to rescue her.
“If a man meets a young woman who is a virgin and not pledged to be married, and he seizes her and lies with her, and they are discovered,
the man who lay with her shall give the young woman’s father 20 ounces of silver,{c} and she shall become his wife, because he has humbled her. He may never divorce her as long as he lives.
“A man shall not take his father’s wife, and so uncover the edge of his father’s garment.{d}

notes.text: Hebrew “become holy,” that is, forfeited to the sanctuary.
Hebrew “a hundred of silver,” that is, 100 shekels, about 40 ounces or 1.15 kilograms.
Hebrew “fifty of silver,” that is, 50 shekels, about 20 ounces or 575 grams.
Verse 30 is 23:1 in the Hebrew text. To “uncover the skirt” of the father is to violate his marriage; compare Ruth 3:9.

verses.text: “No man who has been castrated, whether by crushing or by cutting, may come into the assembly of Yahweh.{a}
No one born of a forbidden union{b} may come into the assembly of Yahweh; not even his offspring to the tenth generation may come into Yahweh’s assembly.
No Ammonite or Moabite may enter the assembly of Yahweh; even to the tenth generation none of them may ever enter the assembly of Yahweh,

because they did not meet you with bread and water on your journey when you came out of Egypt, and because they hired against you Balaam the son of Beor, from Pethor of Aram Naharaim,{c} to curse you.
Yet Yahweh your God refused to heed Balaam, and turned the curse into a blessing for you, because Yahweh your God loved you.
As long as you live, never work for their welfare or their good.
“Do not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother. Do not abhor an Egyptian, because you lived as a foreigner in his land.
Their grandchildren, the third generation born to them, may come into Yahweh’s assembly.
“When you are encamped against your enemies, guard yourself from everything evil.
If any man among you is unclean because of something that happened to him at night, he must go outside the camp; he must not come back into the camp.
When evening comes he shall bathe in water, and at sunset he may come back into the camp.
Mark out a spot outside the camp to which you can go out for your needs.
Among your equipment you shall have a digging tool, and when you squat outside, dig a hole with it and turn back and cover your excrement.
For Yahweh your God moves about within your camp, to deliver you and to give up your enemies before you; so your camp must be holy, that he may see nothing indecent among you and turn away from you.
“Do not hand back to his master a slave who has escaped from his master to you.
Let him live with you, among you, in whatever place he chooses within one of your towns, wherever suits him best. Do not oppress him.
“No Israelite woman is to become a shrine prostitute,{d} and no Israelite man is to become one.
You shall not bring a prostitute’s fee or a dog’s{e} payment into the house of Yahweh your God for any vow, for both are an abomination to Yahweh your God.
“Do not charge your brother interest, whether on money, food, or anything else that may be lent at interest.
You may lend at interest to a foreigner, but to your brother you shall not, that Yahweh your God may bless you in all that you undertake in the land you are entering to possess.
“When you make a vow to Yahweh your God, do not be slow to fulfill it, for Yahweh your God will certainly require it of you, and you would be guilty of sin.
But if you refrain from making a vow, you will not be guilty of sin.
Whatever has passed your lips you must be careful to carry out, just as you freely vowed to Yahweh your God with your own mouth.
“When you go into your neighbor’s vineyard, you may eat as many grapes as you like, until you are full, but you must not put any in your basket.
When you go into the grain field of your neighbor, you may pick ears by hand, but you must not swing a sickle at his standing grain.

notes.text: Verses 1–25 are numbered 2–26 in the Hebrew text.
Hebrew mamzer, a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps one born of incest or of a marriage forbidden by the law.
Aram-naharaim means “Aram of the two rivers,” the region of upper Mesopotamia.
Hebrew qedeshah (feminine) and qadesh (masculine), literally “consecrated one”; the exact practice referred to is debated.
“Dog” probably refers to a male prostitute.

verses.text: “Suppose a man marries a woman, and later she does not find favor in his eyes because he has found in her some matter of indecency, so he writes her a document of divorce, hands it to her, and sends her away from his house.
After leaving his house, she goes off and marries another man.
If the second husband also dislikes her, writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand, and sends her out of his house, or if the second man who married her dies,

then her first husband, who sent her away, may not take her back to be his wife after she has been defiled, for that would be detestable before Yahweh. You must not bring guilt on the land Yahweh your God is giving you as an inheritance.
“When a man has newly married, he shall not go out with the army or be assigned any public duty. He shall be free at home for one year to bring joy to the wife he has taken.
“No one shall take a pair of millstones, or even the upper millstone, as security for a debt, for that would be taking a person’s livelihood{a} as security.
“If a man is caught kidnapping one of his brothers from among the Israelites, and treats him as a slave or sells him, that kidnapper shall die. So you shall burn away the evil from your midst.
“In cases of a skin disease,{b} be very careful to do everything the Levitical priests instruct you. As I commanded them, so you shall take care to do.
Keep in mind how Yahweh your God dealt with Miriam along the road after you left Egypt.
“If you lend anything at all to your neighbor, you must not enter his house to fetch what he offers as a pledge.
Wait outside, and the one who is borrowing from you shall carry the pledge out to you.
And if he is a poor man, do not go to sleep with his pledge.
Be sure to return the pledge to him at sunset, so that he may sleep in his cloak and bless you. It will be counted as righteousness for you before Yahweh your God.
“Do not exploit a hired worker who is poor and needy, whether he is one of your brothers or one of the foreigners who live in your land within your towns.
Give him his wages each day before the sun sets, for he is poor and is counting on it. Otherwise he may cry out against you to Yahweh, and you will be guilty of sin.
“Parents shall not be put to death because of their children, nor children because of their parents; each shall die for his own sin.
“Do not deny justice to the foreigner or the fatherless, and do not take a widow’s garment as security.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt and that Yahweh your God ransomed you from there. For this reason I am commanding you to do this.

“When you harvest the grain of your field and overlook a sheaf there, do not turn back for it. Leave it for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, so that Yahweh your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
When you beat your olive trees, do not go over the branches a second time. What is left shall be for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, do not glean it afterward. What is left shall be for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
You shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt; therefore I am commanding you to do this.

notes.text: Hebrew “life” (nephesh).
Hebrew tsara‘at, traditionally “leprosy,” a term covering various skin diseases; see Leviticus 13–14.

verses.text: “When men have a quarrel and go to law, and the judges hear the case, they shall declare the innocent man in the right and the guilty man in the wrong.
If the one in the wrong deserves a flogging, the judge shall have him laid down and flogged in front of him, with as many lashes as his wrongdoing calls for.
Forty blows may be given him, but no more, or else, if he is beaten with more blows than these, your brother would be degraded in your sight.
“You shall not put a muzzle on the ox as it threshes.

“When brothers live together and one of them dies childless, the widow of the dead man must not marry out of the family to a stranger; her husband’s brother shall come to her and take her to himself as his wife, performing the brother-in-law’s duty{a} toward her.
The firstborn son she bears shall stand in the place of the dead brother and bear his name, so that his name is not erased from Israel.

But if the man has no wish to marry his brother’s wife, she shall go to the gate, to the elders, and tell them, ‘My husband’s brother declines to establish a name in Israel for his brother; he is unwilling to do a brother-in-law’s duty toward me.’
The elders of his town shall then call for him and talk with him. If he stands firm and says, ‘I have no desire to marry her,’

then his brother’s widow is to approach him while the elders watch, draw his sandal from his foot, and spit in his face. And she shall say, ‘So may it be done to the man who refuses to build up his brother’s household.’
And in Israel his family shall be called ‘The House of the Unsandaled.’
“When men are fighting with one another, and the wife of one comes near to rescue her husband from the hand of the man striking him, and she reaches out and seizes him by his private parts,
then you shall cut off her hand. Show her no pity.
“You shall not have two kinds of weights in your bag, one heavy, one light.
Do not keep two different measures in your house, one larger and one smaller.
You shall have a full and honest weight; you shall have a full and honest measure,{b} so that your days may be long in the land Yahweh your God is giving you.
For everyone who does such things, everyone who deals dishonestly, is detestable to Yahweh your God.
“Remember what Amalek did to you on the road as you were coming out of Egypt,
how he met you on the way when you were faint and weary and attacked all the stragglers at your rear. He did not fear God.

So when Yahweh your God gives you rest from all the enemies surrounding you in the land he is giving you to inherit and possess, you are to wipe out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget.

notes.text: Hebrew yabam, the levirate duty, from Latin levir, “husband’s brother.”
Hebrew “ephah,” a dry measure of about 3/5 bushel (22 liters), standing here for measures of capacity in general. Verse 14 likewise has “an ephah and an ephah,” that is, two different measures.

verses.text: “Once you have entered the land Yahweh your God is giving you to inherit, have taken possession of it, and are living there,

you shall take some of the firstfruits of all the produce of the soil which you gather in the land that Yahweh your God is giving you, and put them in a basket, and go to the site where Yahweh your God chooses to settle his name.
You shall go to whoever is priest in those days and say to him, ‘Today I declare to Yahweh your God that I have entered the land that Yahweh swore to our ancestors to give us.’
Then the priest shall take the basket from your hand and set it down before the altar of Yahweh your God.

Then you shall answer in the presence of Yahweh your God, ‘My father was a perishing Aramean.{a} He went down into Egypt and sojourned there, few in number; but there he became a great nation, strong and populous.
But the Egyptians mistreated us, oppressed us, and imposed harsh slavery on us.
Then we cried out to Yahweh, the God of our forefathers, and Yahweh heard our voice and saw our affliction, our toil, and our oppression.
And Yahweh brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, with signs and with wonders.
He led us into this place and has given us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And now, look, I have brought the first of the fruit of the ground that you, Yahweh, have given me.’ Then set it down before Yahweh your God and bow down before Yahweh your God.
And you shall rejoice in all the good that Yahweh your God has given to you and to your household, you and the Levite and the foreigner who is among you.

“When you have completed the tithing of all your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, giving it to the Levite, the sojourner, the orphan, and the widow, that they may eat in your gates and be filled,

then you shall say in the presence of Yahweh your God, ‘I have cleared out of my house the portion that is holy and have handed it over to the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, just as you commanded me. I have not broken or forgotten any of your commands.
I have not eaten of it while mourning, nor removed any of it when unclean, nor given any of it for the dead. I have obeyed Yahweh my God; I have done everything you commanded me.
Look down from your holy dwelling place, from heaven, and bless your people Israel and the ground you have given us, as you swore to our forefathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.’
“This day Yahweh your God commands you to do these statutes and rulings. Be careful to do them with all your heart and with all your soul.
Today you have declared that Yahweh is your God, and that you will walk in his ways, keep his statutes, his commands, and his rulings, and obey his voice.
And Yahweh has declared today that you are a people belonging to him, his own treasure, just as he told you, and that you are to keep all his commands,
and that he will set you high above all the nations he has made, for praise and renown and honor, and that you will be a holy people to Yahweh your God, as he has spoken.”

notes.text: Or “a perishing Aramean” or “an Aramean about to perish,” probably referring to Jacob. The Septuagint reads “My father abandoned Syria.”

verses.text: Then Moses, together with the elders of Israel, gave the people this charge: “Keep the whole command that I am laying on you today.
On the day you cross the Jordan into the land Yahweh your God is giving you, raise up some great stones and coat them with plaster.

When you cross over, inscribe on them every word of this law, so that you may enter the land Yahweh your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, just as Yahweh, the God of your forefathers, promised you.
Once you are across the Jordan, set these stones up on Mount Ebal{a} in keeping with today’s command, and plaster them with plaster.
Build an altar there to Yahweh your God, an altar of stones on which no iron tool has been swung.
Make the altar of Yahweh your God out of whole, unhewn stones, and on it offer up burnt offerings to Yahweh your God.
Offer peace offerings there too, and eat them, and celebrate in the presence of Yahweh your God.
On the stones write every word of this law, clearly and distinctly.”
Then Moses and the Levitical priests addressed all Israel: “Be still, Israel, and hear! This day you have become the people of Yahweh your God.
Therefore listen to the voice of Yahweh your God, and carry out his commands and his statutes, which I am giving you today.”
On the same day Moses also commanded the people:
“After you have crossed the Jordan, these tribes shall take their stand on Mount Gerizim{b} to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
And these shall take their stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
The Levites shall then call out loudly to every man of Israel:

‘A curse on the man who makes an idol, whether carved or cast in metal, a thing Yahweh abhors, made by a craftsman’s hands, and sets it up in a hidden place.’ Then all the people shall respond, ‘Amen.’{c}
‘A curse on anyone who dishonors his father or his mother.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘A curse on anyone who shifts his neighbor’s boundary stone.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘A curse on anyone who makes a blind man lose his way on the road.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘A curse on anyone who twists the justice due to the foreigner, the orphan, or the widow.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘A curse on anyone who lies with his father’s wife, for he has uncovered the edge of his father’s garment.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed be anyone who has intercourse with any animal.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘A curse on anyone who lies with his sister, his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘A curse on anyone who lies with his mother-in-law.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘A curse on anyone who kills his neighbor where no one sees.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘A curse on anyone who accepts a bribe to kill an innocent person.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘A curse on anyone who does not stand by the words of this law and carry them out.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

notes.text: The Samaritan Pentateuch is reported to read “Mount Gerizim” here, and some scholars think that reading may be older; this needs further study.
Gerizim and Ebal are the two mountains on either side of Shechem.
Amen, “so be it,” “surely.”

verses.text: “If you listen faithfully to the voice of Yahweh your God, taking care to keep all his commands that I give you today, Yahweh your God will raise you high above every nation on earth.
All these blessings will come upon you and catch up with you, if you listen to the voice of Yahweh your God:
Blessed will you be in the town, and blessed will you be in the countryside.
Blessed will be the children you bear, the crops of your ground, and the offspring of your animals—the increase of your cattle and the young of your sheep.
Blessed will be your basket and your kneading bowl.
Blessed will you be in your coming in, and blessed in your going out.
“Yahweh will cause your enemies who rise against you to be routed before you. They will march out against you by one road and run from you by seven roads.
Yahweh will command blessing to be with you in your storehouses and on everything you set your hand to; he will bless you in the land that Yahweh your God is giving you.
Yahweh will set you up as his own holy people, just as he swore to you, if you keep the commandments of Yahweh your God and walk in his ways.
Then all the peoples of the earth will see that you are called by the name of Yahweh,{a} and they will stand in fear of you.
Yahweh will give you an abundance of good things—in the fruit of your womb, in the young of your livestock, and in the yield of your soil—in the land Yahweh swore to your forefathers to give you.

Yahweh will open for you his rich storehouse, the heavens, to send rain on your land in its season and to bless all the work of your hands. You will lend to many nations, and you yourself will borrow from none.
Yahweh will make you the head, not the tail; you will be only above, and never beneath, if you obey the commandments of Yahweh your God, which I am commanding you today, to observe and do them,
and if you do not turn aside to the right or to the left from any of the words I command you today, to go after other gods and serve them.

“But if you will not listen to the voice of Yahweh your God, and are not careful to keep all his commands and statutes that I give you today, then all these curses will come upon you and catch up with you:
Cursed will you be in the town, and cursed will you be in the countryside.
Cursed will be your basket and your kneading bowl.
Cursed shall be your offspring, the produce of your soil, the increase of your herds, and the young of your flocks.
Cursed will you be in your coming in, and cursed in your going out.

“Yahweh will send against you curse, panic, and frustration in everything you set your hand to do, until you are wiped out and perish swiftly because of the evil of your deeds, because you have abandoned me.
Yahweh will make the plague cling to you until he has made an end of you in the land you are entering to possess.
Yahweh will strike you with wasting disease, with fever, inflammation, burning heat, and drought,{b} with blight and with mildew. They will hound you until you perish.
The sky over your head will be bronze, and the earth beneath you iron.
Yahweh will turn the rain of your land into powder and dust; it will come down on you from the sky until you are destroyed.
“Yahweh will let you be beaten before your enemies. You will go out against them by one road and flee before them by seven roads, and you will become a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
Your corpses will be food for every bird of the sky and every beast of the earth, and no one will frighten them away.
Yahweh will strike you with the boils of Egypt, with tumors, with scabs, and with an itch that cannot be cured.
Yahweh will strike you with madness, blindness, and confusion of mind.
At midday you will feel your way like a blind man in darkness, and your paths will lead nowhere. Day after day you will be oppressed and plundered, and there will be no one to save you.
You will pledge yourself to a woman, and another man will lie with her. You will build a house and never dwell in it. You will plant a vineyard and not taste its grapes.

Your ox will be slaughtered in front of you, yet none of its meat will reach your mouth. Your donkey will be seized in front of you and never come back. Your sheep will be given to your enemies, and there will be no one to help you.
Your sons and daughters will be given to another people while you watch, and your eyes will wear themselves out longing for them all day, but your hand will be powerless.
A people you have not known will eat up the fruit of your land and all your labor, and you will be nothing but oppressed and crushed all your days.
The sights your eyes see will drive you mad.
Yahweh will strike you on the knees and legs with painful boils that cannot be healed, from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head.
“Yahweh will bring you and the king you set over yourself to a nation that neither you nor your forefathers have known, and there you will serve other gods, of wood and stone.
You will become an object of horror, a proverb, and a byword among all the peoples to which Yahweh will drive you.
You will carry much seed out to the field and gather in little, because the locust will devour it.
You will plant vineyards and tend them, but you will neither drink the wine nor gather the grapes, because the worm will eat them.
Olive trees you will have all through your borders, but there will be no oil for you to rub on yourself, for the olives will fall off unripe.
You will father sons and daughters, but they will not remain yours, for they will go into captivity.
The whirring locust will take over all your trees and the fruit of your ground.
The foreigner who lives among you will climb higher and higher above you, while you sink lower and lower.
He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail.

“All these curses will come upon you, pursuing you and overtaking you until you are destroyed, because you did not listen to the voice of Yahweh your God or keep the commands and statutes he gave you.
They will be a sign and a wonder upon you and your descendants forever.
Because you did not serve Yahweh your God with joy and gladness of heart when you had plenty of everything,
you will serve your enemies whom Yahweh sends against you, in hunger and thirst, in nakedness, and lacking everything. He will put an iron yoke on your neck until he has destroyed you.
Yahweh will raise against you a nation from far off, from the ends of the earth, swift as an eagle in its dive, a nation that speaks a tongue you do not understand,
a fierce-faced nation that shows no regard for the old and no mercy to the young.

It will eat the young of your livestock and the yield of your soil until you are destroyed. It will leave you no grain, new wine, or oil, no calves of your herds or lambs of your flock, until it has brought you to ruin.

It will lay siege to you in all your towns until the high, fortified walls you trust in come down throughout your land. It will besiege you in all your towns throughout the land Yahweh your God has given you.
Then, in the siege and in the distress your enemy brings on you, you will eat the fruit of your own womb, the flesh of the sons and daughters whom Yahweh your God has given you.
Even the most gentle and refined man among you will look grudgingly at his brother, at the wife he embraces, and at the last of his children who remain,
refusing to give any of them the flesh of his children that he is eating, because nothing else is left to him in the siege and distress your enemy will inflict on you in all your towns.

The tender and delicate woman among you, so tender and delicate that she would not try to put the sole of her foot on the ground, will begrudge the husband she cherishes, and her son and her daughter,

and at the afterbirth that comes out from between her feet and the children she bears, for she will eat them secretly for lack of anything else, in the siege and distress your enemy will inflict on you in your towns.
“If you do not take care to observe all the words of this law written in this book, and to revere this glorious and awesome name, Yahweh your God,
then Yahweh will bring extraordinary plagues on you and your descendants, great and lasting plagues, and grievous and lasting illnesses.
He will bring upon you again every disease of Egypt that terrified you, and they will hold you fast.
Yahweh will also bring on you every sickness and every plague not written in this book of the law, until you are destroyed.
Though you were as numerous as the stars in the sky, you will be left few in number, because you did not listen to the voice of Yahweh your God.

And just as Yahweh took delight in prospering you and increasing your number, so Yahweh will take delight in bringing you to ruin and destroying you; and you shall be plucked from the land you are entering to possess.
“Yahweh will scatter you among all peoples, from one end of the earth to the other, and there you will serve other gods of wood and stone that neither you nor your forefathers have known.
Among those nations you will find no ease, no resting place for the sole of your foot. Instead Yahweh will give you there a trembling heart, failing eyes, and a despairing soul.
Your life shall hang in suspense before you; night and day you shall be in terror, with no assurance of your life.
At daybreak you will say, ‘Would that evening were here!’ and at nightfall, ‘Would that morning were here!’ because of the terror gripping your heart and the things your eyes will see.

And Yahweh will return you to Egypt in ships, by the route I told you you would never see again; and there you will be put up for sale to your enemies as male and female slaves, but there will be no buyer.”

notes.text: Hebrew “that the name of Yahweh is called over you,” an expression of ownership.
Or “sword,” following a different vocalization of the Hebrew.

verses.text: These are the words of the covenant Yahweh commanded Moses to make with the Israelites in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant he made with them at Horeb.{a}
Moses summoned all Israel and said to them: “You have seen everything Yahweh did before your eyes in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh and all his servants and his whole land—
the great trials your eyes saw, the signs, and those great wonders.
Yet even now Yahweh has not given you a mind that understands, eyes that see, or ears that hear.
I led you forty years in the wilderness. Your clothes did not wear out on you, and your sandals did not wear out on your feet.
You ate no bread and drank no wine or strong drink, so that you might know that I am Yahweh your God.
And when you reached this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan marched out to meet us in battle, and we struck them down.
We seized their land and handed it over as an inheritance to Reuben, to Gad, and to half the tribe of Manasseh.
Therefore observe the words of this covenant and do them, that you may succeed in all that you do.
“All of you are standing today before Yahweh your God—your leaders, your tribes, your elders, and your officers, every man of Israel,
your little ones, your wives, and the foreigner in your camp, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water—
so that you may enter into the covenant of Yahweh your God, sealed with an oath, which Yahweh your God is making with you today,
in order to establish you today as his people, and that he may be your God, as he promised you and as he swore to your forefathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
And I am making this covenant and this oath not only with you,
but with those who stand here with us today in the presence of Yahweh our God, and also with those who are not here with us today.
“You know how we lived in the land of Egypt and how we passed through the midst of the nations you passed through.
You saw their abominations and their idols of wood and stone, silver and gold, which were among them.

Beware, lest there be among you a man or woman, family or tribe, whose heart turns away today from Yahweh our God to go and serve the gods of those nations; lest there be among you a root that produces gall and bitterness,

someone who, on hearing the words of this oath, blesses himself in his heart, thinking, ‘I will be safe, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart,’ bringing ruin on watered and dry land alike.{b}

Yahweh will not be willing to forgive him. Instead the anger and jealousy of Yahweh will smoke against that man, and every curse written in this book will settle on him, and Yahweh will blot out his name from under heaven.
Yahweh will single him out from all the tribes of Israel for disaster, according to all the curses of the covenant written in this book of the law.

And the generation to come, your children who rise up after you, and the foreigner who comes from a distant land, will see the plagues of that land and the sicknesses with which Yahweh has afflicted it—

the whole land burned out with sulfur and salt, nothing sown, nothing sprouting, no plant growing in it, an overthrow like that of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which Yahweh overthrew in his anger and wrath—
and all the nations will say, ‘Why has Yahweh done this to this land? What was the reason for this great burning anger?’
Then people will say, ‘It is because they abandoned the covenant of Yahweh, the God of their forefathers, which he made with them when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.
They went and served other gods and worshiped them, gods they had not known and that he had not allotted to them.
That is why Yahweh’s anger blazed against this land, so that he brought upon it all the curses recorded in this book.
And Yahweh uprooted them from their land in anger and fury and great indignation, and flung them into another land, as it is this day.’
“The hidden things belong to Yahweh our God, but the things revealed belong to us and to our children forever,{c} so that we may do all the words of this law.

notes.text: Verse 1 is 28:69 in the Hebrew text, and verses 2–29 are numbered 1–28.
Hebrew “to sweep away the watered with the dry,” probably a proverb meaning total destruction.
In the Hebrew text the words “to us and to our children” are marked with extraordinary dots (puncta extraordinaria), whose meaning is uncertain.

verses.text: “When all these things have come upon you, the blessing and the curse I have set before you, and you call them to mind among all the nations where Yahweh your God has driven you,
and you return to Yahweh your God and listen to his voice in everything I command you today, you and your children, with all your heart and with all your soul,
then Yahweh your God will bring back your captives{a} and have mercy on you; he will gather you again from all the peoples where Yahweh your God has dispersed you.
Even if your exiles are at the far edge of the sky, from there Yahweh your God will gather you, and from there he will fetch you.
Yahweh your God will bring you into the land your forefathers possessed, and you will possess it. He will do you good and make you more numerous than your forefathers.
And Yahweh your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your descendants, so that you will love Yahweh your God with your whole heart and your whole soul, in order that you may live.
And Yahweh your God will lay all these curses on your enemies and on those who hate and persecute you.
You will again obey the voice of Yahweh and keep all his commands that I give you today.

Yahweh your God will make you overflow with good things in all the work of your hands, in the children you bear, in the young of your animals, and in the crops of your ground. For Yahweh will again take delight in your welfare, as he delighted in your forefathers,

when you listen to the voice of Yahweh your God by keeping his commands and his statutes written in this book of the law, and when you turn to Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
“This command I give you today is not too hard for you, nor is it out of your reach.
It is not up in the heavens, so that you should say, ‘Who will climb up to heaven for us and bring it down to us, and tell it to us so that we may do it?’
Nor is it beyond the sea, so that you need ask, ‘Who will go across the sea on our behalf, bring it to us, and have us hear it, so that we may do it?’
No, the word is very close to you, in your mouth and in your heart, so that you can do it.
“See, today I have laid before you life and good, death and evil.

For I command you today to love Yahweh your God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commands, his statutes, and his rulings, so that you may live and multiply, and Yahweh your God will bless you in the land you are entering to possess.{b}
But if your heart turns away and you refuse to listen, and you are drawn off to bow to other gods and serve them,
I declare to you today that you shall surely perish; you will not prolong your days on the soil that you cross the Jordan to enter and possess.
I call heaven and earth to witness against you today: I have set before you life and death, blessing and curse. So choose life, that you and your descendants may live,

loving Yahweh your God, listening to his voice, and holding fast to him. For he is your life and the length of your days, so that you may dwell in the land Yahweh swore to give to your forefathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.”

notes.text: Or “bring you back from captivity.”
The Septuagint begins this verse, “If you hearken to the commandments of the Lord your God, which I command you this day” (Brenton, modernized), a clause missing from the traditional Hebrew text.

verses.text: Then Moses went and spoke{a} these words to all Israel.
And he said to them, “Today I am one hundred twenty years old; I can no longer go out and come in, and Yahweh has said to me, ‘You shall not cross this Jordan.’

Yahweh your God is the one who will go across in front of you. It is he who will wipe out these nations before you so that you take their place. And Joshua will lead you across, just as Yahweh has said.
And Yahweh will deal with them as he dealt with Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, and with their land, which he destroyed.
Yahweh will hand them over to you, and you must treat them exactly as the command I have given you requires.
Be strong and brave. Do not fear them or tremble before them, for it is Yahweh your God who goes with you. He will not let you go or abandon you.”

Then Moses called Joshua and said to him in the sight of all Israel, “Be strong and brave, for you will go with this people into the land Yahweh swore to their forefathers to give them, and you will divide it among them as their inheritance.
Yahweh himself goes before you; he will be with you. He will not let you go or abandon you. Do not be afraid or dismayed.”
Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of Yahweh’s covenant, and to all the elders of Israel.
Then Moses gave them this command: “Every seventh year, at the set time of the year when debts are released, during the Feast of Booths,{b}
when all Israel comes to appear in the presence of Yahweh your God at the place he will choose, you shall read this law before all Israel, in their hearing.
Assemble the people, men, women, and children, and the sojourner in your gates, so that they may listen and learn to revere Yahweh your God and be careful to observe every word of this law,
and that their children, who have not known it, may listen and learn to revere Yahweh your God as long as you live in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess.”

Then Yahweh said to Moses, “Your time to die is drawing near. Summon Joshua, and both of you take your stand in the tent of meeting, and I will give him his charge.” So Moses and Joshua went and stood in the tent of meeting.
And Yahweh appeared at the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stood over the entrance of the tent.

Yahweh said to Moses, “Soon you will lie down to rest with your forefathers, and this people will rise up and go whoring after the alien gods of the land into which they are going. They will abandon me and break the covenant I made with them.

My anger will be kindled against them on that day, and I will forsake them and conceal my face from them; they will be consumed, and many disasters and distresses will befall them. And they will say on that day, ‘Have not these disasters come upon us because our God is not in our midst?’
On that day I will indeed turn my face away from them, on account of all the wickedness they have committed by turning to other gods.
“Now therefore write this song for yourselves, and teach it to the Israelites; put it in their mouths, that this song may be a witness for me against the Israelites.

For I will bring them into the land flowing with milk and honey that I promised on oath to their forefathers, and when they have eaten until they are full and have become fat, they will go after other gods and serve them, scorning me and breaking my covenant.

And when many evils and troubles have found them, this song will testify against them as a witness, for it will not be forgotten from the mouths of their offspring. For I know the plans they are forming even today, before I have brought them into the land I swore to give.”
So Moses wrote this song down on that day and taught it to the Israelites.
And Yahweh{c} commissioned Joshua the son of Nun and said, “Be strong and courageous, for you shall bring the Israelites into the land that I swore to them, and I will be with you.”
When Moses had finished writing the words of this law in a book, to the very end,
he gave this command to the Levites, the bearers of the ark of Yahweh’s covenant:
“Take this book of the law and put it beside the ark of the covenant of Yahweh your God, so that it may stay there as a witness against you.
For I know how rebellious and stiff-necked you are. If even today, while I am still alive among you, you have been rebels against Yahweh, how much more after my death!
Gather to me all the elders of your tribes and your officials, that I may speak these words in their ears and call heaven and earth to witness against them.

For I know that after my death you will act very corruptly and turn aside from the way I have commanded you. Disaster will meet you in later days, because you will do what Yahweh regards as evil, and anger him through what your hands have made.”
Then, while the whole assembly of Israel listened, Moses spoke the words of this song from beginning to end:

notes.text: The Septuagint reads “Moses finished speaking” (Brenton), and a Qumran manuscript is reported to agree; the difference involves two similar Hebrew words.
Held in the seventh month, Tishri (September–October).
Hebrew “he”; the context shows that Yahweh is meant. The Septuagint makes Moses the subject.

verses.text: “Give ear, you heavens, and I will speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
Let my teaching fall like rain, my speech settle like the dew, like fine showers on new grass, like heavy rains on the green plants.
For I will proclaim the name of Yahweh; give greatness to our God!
“The Rock—his work is perfect; all his ways are justice. A God of faithfulness and without wrong, righteous and upright is he.
Acting corruptly toward him, they are no longer his children, because of their blemish;{a} a perverse and crooked generation.
Is this how you repay Yahweh, you foolish and unwise people? Is he not your father, who acquired you,{b} who made you and established you?
“Remember the days of long ago; consider the years of generations past. Ask your father, and he will inform you, your elders, and they will tell you.
When the Most High{c} gave the nations their inheritance, when he divided the descendants of Adam,{d} he fixed the borders of the peoples according to the number of the sons of Israel.{e}
For Yahweh’s portion is his people, Jacob his allotted inheritance.
“He found him in a desert land, in an empty, howling waste. He encircled him and watched over him; he guarded him like the pupil{f} of his eye.
Like an eagle that rouses its nest and hovers over its young, he spread out his wings and took him up, bearing him on his pinions.
Yahweh by himself was his guide; there was no alien god beside him.
He made him ride on the heights of the land, and he ate the produce of the field. He fed him honey from the rock and oil from the flinty crag,
curds from the herd and milk from the flock, with the fat of lambs, rams of Bashan’s breed and he-goats, with the choicest kernels of wheat; and you drank wine, the foaming blood of the grape.
“But Jeshurun{g} grew fat and kicked— you grew fat, you grew bloated and gorged— he abandoned the God who made him and scorned the Rock of his salvation.
They made him jealous with strange gods; they angered him with detestable things.
They sacrificed to demons that were no god, to gods they had never known, to new gods lately arrived, whom your forefathers never dreaded.
You neglected the Rock that begot you, and forgot the God who gave you birth.
“Yahweh saw it and spurned them, provoked by his sons and his daughters.
He said, ‘I will hide my face from them; I will see what their end will be, for they are a perverse generation, children with no faithfulness in them.
They roused my jealousy with a no-god; they angered me with their empty idols.{h} So I will rouse their jealousy with a no-people; I will anger them with a nation that lacks sense.
For fire has flared up in my anger, and it burns down to the depths of Sheol;{i} it consumes the earth and its harvest and sets the roots of the mountains ablaze.
“ ‘I will pile up evils on them; I will spend every arrow I have against them.
They will be wasted by hunger, devoured by plague and bitter pestilence. I will send the fangs of wild beasts against them, with the venom of things that glide in the dust.
Outside, the sword will bereave, and in the inner rooms, terror, for young man and virgin alike, for the nursing infant and the gray-haired man.
I said, “I will scatter them,{j} I will erase their memory from among mankind,”
but I feared the taunting of the enemy, that their foes might misjudge and say, “Our hand has prevailed; Yahweh did not do any of this.” ’
“For they are a nation void of counsel, and there is no understanding in them.
If they were wise, they would grasp this; they would see what their end will be.
How could a single man pursue a thousand, and two drive ten thousand into flight, unless their Rock had sold them, unless Yahweh had given them up?
For their rock is not like our Rock— even our enemies are judges of that.
For their vine comes from the vine of Sodom and from the terraces of Gomorrah; their grapes are full of poison; their clusters taste of bitterness.
Their wine is the venom of serpents, the cruel poison of vipers.
“ ‘Is this not stored away with me, sealed up in my treasuries?
Vengeance and recompense are mine,{k} for the time when their foot shall slip; for their day of calamity is at hand, and their doom comes swiftly.’
For Yahweh will judge his people and relent concerning his servants, when he sees that their power has vanished and none remain, whether bound or free.
Then he will say, ‘Where are their gods, the rock in which they sought refuge,
who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their drink offerings? Let them get up and help you; let them be a shelter over you!
“‘See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god beside me; I am the one who puts to death and gives life; I have wounded, and I myself heal, and none can deliver from my hand.
For I raise my hand to heaven and say, As I live forever,
once I whet my lightning sword and my hand grasps judgment, I will pay back vengeance to my foes and repay those who hate me.
I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will feed on flesh, with the blood of the slain and the captives, from the heads of the long-haired leaders of the enemy.’{l}
“Shout for joy, you nations, over his people,{m} for he will avenge the blood of his servants. He will pay back vengeance to his foes and make atonement for his land and his people.”{n}
Moses came and recited all the words of this song in the ears of the people, he and Hoshea{o} son of Nun.
When Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel,
he said to them, “Set your hearts on all the words I testify to you today, so that you may command your children to take care to do every word of this law.
For this is no empty word for you; it is your very life. Through this word your days will be long on the soil you are going over the Jordan to possess.”
That same day Yahweh spoke to Moses:
“Go up this Abarim mountain range,{p} to Mount Nebo, in the land of Moab across from Jericho, and look at the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites for a possession;
and die on the mountain you are about to ascend, and be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people,
because you both broke faith with me among the Israelites at the waters of Meribah-kadesh{q} in the Wilderness of Zin, by failing to uphold my holiness among the Israelites.
You will see the land from a distance, but you will not go into the land I am giving to the Israelites.”

notes.text: The Hebrew of this line is obscure. The Septuagint reads “spotted children” (Brenton).
Or “created you.”
Hebrew ‘Elyon, a title of God meaning “highest.”
Or “humankind”; Hebrew “the sons of Adam.”

So the traditional Hebrew text (MT). A Hebrew manuscript from Qumran (4QDeut-j) reads “the sons of God,” and many scholars regard that as the earlier reading. The Septuagint reads “the angels of God” (Brenton), and some Greek manuscripts are reported to read “the sons of God.” The difference bears on whether the nations are allotted to heavenly beings under the Most High (compare 4:19; 29:26). This needs scholarly review.
Hebrew “the little man of his eye.”
Jeshurun means “upright one,” a poetic name for Israel. The Septuagint reads “So Jacob ate and was filled, and the beloved one kicked” (Brenton).
Hebrew hebel, “vapor” or “breath.”
Sheol is the realm of the dead.
Hebrew uncertain; perhaps “cut them in pieces” or “blow them away.”
The Septuagint reads “In the day of vengeance I will recompense” (Brenton). Romans 12:19 and Hebrews 10:30 quote this line as “Vengeance is mine; I will repay.”
Or “from the heads of the enemy’s leaders.”
Or “Praise his people, you nations.” The traditional Hebrew wording is brief and can be read several ways.

This verse is much longer in other ancient witnesses. The Septuagint reads (Brenton, modernized): “Rejoice, you heavens, with him, and let all the angels of God worship him; rejoice, you Gentiles, with his people, and let all the sons of God strengthen themselves in him; for he will avenge the blood of his sons, and he will render vengeance, and recompense justice to his enemies, and will reward those who hate him; and the Lord shall purge the land of his people.” A Hebrew manuscript from Qumran (4QDeut-q) is reported to have a longer text than the traditional Hebrew as well, including a call to the heavens to rejoice and to the gods (or heavenly beings) to bow down to him. Hebrews 1:6 and Romans 15:10 appear to draw on the longer form. This needs scholarly review.

Hoshea means “salvation,” the earlier name of Joshua (Numbers 13:16). The Septuagint reads “Joshua” (Brenton, “Joshua the son of Naue”), and it also begins the verse, “And Moses wrote this song in that day, and taught it to the children of Israel.”
Abarim means “regions beyond,” the range east of the Jordan facing Jericho.
Meribah means “quarreling”; see Numbers 20:1–13.

verses.text: Here is the blessing which Moses, the man of God, spoke over the Israelites before he died.
He said: “Yahweh came from Sinai, and rose from Seir upon them; he shone forth from Mount Paran, and came with ten thousands of holy ones;{a} at his right hand was a flaming fire{b} for them.
Truly he loves the peoples;{c} all his holy ones are in your hand. They sit at your feet, each receiving your words.
Moses gave us a law, a possession for the assembly of Jacob.
And there was a king in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people gathered, the tribes of Israel together.
“Let Reuben live and not die, though his men be few.”
And this he said for Judah: “Hear, Yahweh, the voice of Judah, and bring him in to his people. With his own hands he fights for his cause;{d} be his help against his foes.”
For Levi he said: “Your Thummim and your Urim{e} belong to your faithful man, whom you tested at Massah, with whom you strove at the waters of Meribah;
who said of his father and of his mother, ‘I regard them not’; he did not acknowledge his brothers, nor know his own children. For they have observed your word and kept your covenant.
They teach your rulings to Jacob and your law to Israel; they set incense before you{f} and whole burnt offerings on your altar.
Bless, Yahweh, his strength, and take pleasure in the work of his hands. Smash the loins of his attackers, of those who hate him, so that they rise no more.”
For Benjamin he said: “The one Yahweh loves dwells in safety beside him. He shelters him all day long, and he rests between his shoulders.”{g}
For Joseph he said: “May his land be blessed by Yahweh with the choicest gifts of heaven, the dew, and of the deep that crouches below,
with the choicest yield of the sun and the rich produce of the months,{h}
with the finest things of the ancient mountains and the wealth of the hills that last forever,
and with the choicest gifts of the earth and its fullness, and the good will of him who lived in the bush. May they come on the head of Joseph, on the brow of the prince among his brothers.

His firstborn bull has majesty, and his horns are the horns of the wild ox; with them he shall gore peoples, every one, to earth’s farthest limits; they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh.”
For Zebulun he said: “Rejoice, Zebulun, as you go out, and you, Issachar, in your tents.
They will summon peoples to the mountain; there they will offer right sacrifices, for they will draw on the wealth of the seas and the treasures hidden in the sand.”
For Gad he said: “Blessed be the one who makes Gad’s land wide! Gad lies in wait like a lioness and tears off arm and scalp alike.
He chose the first part for himself, for a ruler’s portion was kept for him there. He came with the heads of the people; he carried out the justice of Yahweh and his rulings for Israel.”
For Dan he said: “Dan is a lion’s whelp that springs out from Bashan.”
For Naphtali he said: “Naphtali, filled with favor and full of Yahweh’s blessing, take possession of the sea{i} and the south.”
For Asher he said: “Asher is blessed above the other sons; let his brothers look on him with favor, and may he bathe his feet in oil.
Your bolts will be of iron and bronze, and your strength{j} will last as long as your days.
“There is none like God, Jeshurun, who rides the heavens to your aid, and the clouds in his majesty.
The God of old is your dwelling place,{k} and underneath are the arms that last forever. He drove out the enemy before you and said, ‘Destroy!’
So Israel dwells in safety, the spring of Jacob undisturbed,{l} in a land of grain and new wine, where the heavens drip with dew.

How happy you are, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by Yahweh, the shield that helps you and the sword of your triumph? Your enemies will come cringing to you, and you will tread upon their high places.”{m}

notes.text: Or “from Ribeboth-kodesh,” perhaps a place name. The Septuagint reads “with the ten thousands of Kadesh” (Brenton, “Cades”).

The Urim and Thummim were the priestly lots used to seek God’s will; the names may mean “lights” and “perfections.” The Septuagint begins, “Give to Levi” (Brenton), and a Qumran manuscript is reported to read similarly.

Or “moons.”
Or “the west.” Hebrew yam can mean “sea” or “west”; here perhaps the Sea of Galilee.

verses.text: Then Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the summit of Pisgah, which faces Jericho, and Yahweh showed him the whole land: Gilead as far as Dan,
all of Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah up to the sea in the west,{a}
the Negev,{b} and the plain of the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees, as far as Zoar.

Then Yahweh said to him, “This is the land I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob when I said, ‘To your offspring I will give it.’ I have shown it to you, and you have seen it, but you yourself will not go over there.”
So Moses, the servant of Yahweh, died there in the land of Moab, as Yahweh had said.{c}
And he buried him{d} in the valley in the land of Moab opposite Beth Peor; but his burial place is unknown to this day.”
Moses was 120 years old when he died. His sight had not grown dim, and his vigor had not left him.
The Israelites mourned for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days, until the days of weeping in mourning for Moses were complete.
Now Joshua son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, since Moses had placed his hands upon him, and the Israelites obeyed him and did what Yahweh had commanded Moses.
Never since has a prophet arisen in Israel like Moses, whom Yahweh knew face to face,
none like him for all the signs and wonders Yahweh sent him to perform in Egypt against Pharaoh and against all his officials and his whole land,
and for all the mighty deeds and all the great and awesome acts that Moses did in the sight of all Israel.

notes.text: That is, the Mediterranean.
Negev means “dry land,” the arid south of Judah.
Hebrew “at the mouth of Yahweh.” Later Jewish tradition read this as “by the kiss of Yahweh.”
That is, Yahweh buried him. Or “he was buried.” The Septuagint reads “they buried him” (Brenton).
